product_title: Dean Exotica Quilt Ash Acoustic-Electric 12 String Guitar, Gloss Natural
review_headline: Great plugged in, not so great as a standalone acoustic
review_body:
I've been playing fingerstyle acoustic for a little over 25 years and haven't touched 12 string in quite a while so decided the price range and reviews on this guitar seemed to be what I was looking for so why not give it a go? I have a nice top of the line 6 string I've been using the past 10 years but can't afford a top of the line 12 right now so figured I'd start at the less-than-$500 range and see what happened.

Pros: Great action right out of the box, easy to play, stays in tune, and sounds great plugged in.

That's where the buck stopped for me.

Cons: Unplugged it sounds dull and lifeless. I read another review where the player mentioned this but chose to ignore it and try it myself based on all of the other great reviews. The body/bracing and \\"gloss\\" is way too sturdy and solid for an acoustic build so you feel almost no resonance in the body while you play it which sadly is where most of the characteristics of an acoustic come from. It sounds very boxy, quiet and shallow. It was barely loud enough to keep up with a hand drum and fretless bass. Also there were visible glue drips you could clearly see when looking into the soundhole of the guitar. Not the end of the world but annoying nonetheless.

In a nutshell although some may find these >$1K \\"exotic wood\\" guitars to be real purdy it seems that the crazy wood, bridge shapes, and binding are there as a deterrent from the lack of quality in nearly all other areas as far as acoustic guitars are concerned. I would have been severely disappointed if I'd paid full price for the one I tried, but thankfully I only paid $300 for a b-stock model. Which in my opinion is still too much $ for this guitar. I ended up finding an incredible deal on an all around awesome acoustic/electric 12 string + case for not much more via Craigslist. The second I played it I knew the Dean was going to get boxed up and returned.

This isn't a knock on Dean guitars whatsoever, I've loved a few of their electrics I've played. And as mentioned, the guitar I tried out had great action and sounded beautiful plugged in. But I needed it to behave and sound like an acoustic too which this guitar just doesn't do. I felt the need to write an honest review and balance out all of the glaring 5 star reviews/comments and write this off as an \\"if it sounds too good to be true than it probably is\\" experience. Kudos to you other reviewers if it worked out for you, but to other buyers seriously considering one of these either try one in person or make sure where you buy from has a generous return policy.

product_title: Auralex Acoustics MoPAD-XL Monitor Acoustic Isolation Pads, 2" x 8.75" x 12",  1 Pair, Charcoal
review_body:
In a nutshell: the \\"SpeakerDudes\\" really do work and, although they may just be a couple of foam pads, you will not regret spending forty bucks to get a pair.

I have a pair of m-audio bx5's on my desk and listen to plenty of jazz, mostly streamed via my laptop, with the low end boosted a bit so I can follow the great bass lines from my favorites like Ron Carter, Eddie Gomez, Steve Swallow, Dave Holland, Charlie Haden, Gary Peacock... you get the picture. The bx-5's are not the greatest speakers on Planet Earth, but for well-priced, self-powered nearfield monitors they are capable of producing reasonably pure and powerful sound - except for a somewhat muddy mess at the bottom when they are placed directly on a wooden desktop.

Like many others, for a long time I looked at these Auralex \\"isolation platforms\\" and thought it made no sense to pay $40 or more for a pair of foam pads. That was a dumb cheapskate thing to do. Having just received and tried out a new set of \\"SpeakerDudes,\\" I can report that it is $40 well spent. It might well be possible to fabricate a pair of these myself and save a bit of do re mi, but if one factors in the cost of high density foam of the type Auralex uses, the time to find the stuff and make a pair of platforms - well, it isn't worth fussing over the price. Plus I am sure I could not sculpt a pair of platforms, like these, that can be easily oriented to tilt the speakers facing slightly up, down, or parallel to my desk top - and if I were to try the DIY route, mine surely would not look as polished as these do.

The sound? Believe it. These isolation pads make a significant difference - particularly down at the bottom, where direct contact with a wood desktop otherwise creates resonances that boom and blur rapid runs on a plucked upright or electric bass.

Just quit bellyaching about the $40 and, if you care about getting the best sound from your bookshelf or desktop speakers, buy these andenjoy.

review_headline: Good sound for the price, comfort is questionable though.
review_body: The sound quality is commendable. The high and mids are crisp, clear and well defined. It is a little lacking in the bass though. My greatest complaint is in the comfort for longevity. These headphones are extremely tight. Im 6'4\\" tall and 230lb. I do not have an abnormally large head. These headphones fit very snugly. After about 2 hours they begin to get uncomfortable to a point where you are repositioning them on your head. The pressure around your ears is where the discomfort is greatest. The sound isolation is absolutely excellent though. I have a very loud air cooled PC right next to me and it is completely deadened by these phones. If you are larger than average, like me, perhaps consider another brand/model. I have worn these for about 2-3 weeks and have yet to experience a stretching out, or easing of tightness like I have read will happen.

product_title: TASCAM DR-40 4-Track Portable Digital Recorder BRONZE
review_body:
I just got through putting this thing through it's paces.
*Internal Mics: For the price, the internal mics are fantastic. There is a lot of handling noise, and that is the result of the cheap, hard plastic body. The H4n is definitely sturdier. The mics look like solid metal, but they're cheap plastic as well. All that said, they pick up warm, rich sound, especially for the price point.
*Build quality: It feels like a cheap plastic toy. The H4n is much sturdier, but then the H4n is more expensive. The buttons on the Tascam feel pretty sturdy, though.
Internal Preamps: Yeah, if you're a newbie to sound recording like me, you may not even know what that means. Basically, it's the device(s) inside the recorder that boosts the electric signal coming into the recorder from an outside source, like a microphone. The Preamps on this are really weak. I tried using my Sony EOS-44b Lavalier mic (pro grade lapel mic), and there was a lot of hissing noise, even with the Gain turned down (but then I didn't get a good signal that way). I then tried a Sennheiser EW112PG3A Wireless Kit. The sound was great with this set up, but the Sennheiser is delivers a more powerful signal. So, higher power mics are going to be fine on the Tascam, but low power mics won't.
*Learning Curve: 5 minutes. Seriously. It's really easy to learn if you just click around and try combinations of buttons. I only had to refer to the handbook for one thing. That said, in the age of smart phone touch screens, the LCD setup on this seems like something from the stone age. Again... the price point on this was really low for sound equipment.

All in all, I just don't think there's anything else out there that's even close to this price point that will deliver better results. Get the right gear to go with it, but it works like a champ.

product_title: Cremona Premier Novice Violin
review_headline: It works for practicing, but not great for anything else
review_body:
You can't expect much from a violin this cheap, so I hate to do this- but I'm going to start off by listing all of the things wrong with this violin. The neck of the violin is cracked, not from shipping, but from factory because the crack was varnished over. The paint was scuffed and scratched in a couple places, and the bridge was displaced pretty badly (easily fixed though). The last thing, is the bow is extremely warped to the left side with a little twist in it, so the tip is not aligned with the grip making it very difficult to play with a straight arm. It was also a real pain to tune, and keep it tuned. It's pretty useless. It is, however, a very attractive looking violin and it does have a really good sound to it once finally tuned right. Overall, it's a great practice violin for beginners on a budget. Also, from what I can tell it's the same violin as the Cecilio, so for a few extra bucks you'll get a second bow, extra strings, extra bridge, a tuner etc. so go with the Cecilio as it is the same violin with a different brand name.

Update:
Only took a couple days of playing, and the nut on the fingerboard cracked on the E string. Now I will have to replace the nut before it is playable again. The strings have already stretched too much, so if you buy this violin, be sure to replace strings with better quality ones.

product_title: Samson MS100 Studio Monitor Stands
review_headline: Single-handedly the worst product I have ever purchased. Anywhere.
review_body:
I have always been somewhat careful with my purchases, but seeing as many other monitor stands were very expensive, a $70 pair seemed like a good deal. After receiving this product, however, I quickly realized that I'd feel safer suspending my monitors with Silly Putty over a medieval spike pit than I would letting them rest on these stands. The product design and the disgraceful build quality are so, so disgustingly poor that you feel completely scammed. There is absolutely no way anybody can look at these and think \\"they can certainly support monitor speakers, I should sell them!\\" No -- the intent here is to take advantage of you.

Judging from the product image, you'd assume that the top of the stand, which supports the monitor itself, is a flat, rigid plate that is tightly secured to the vertical column. However, these guys are crafty -- they took their product image such that the tops of the stands show only the side profile, in order to hide the stupidity that would otherwise be visible.

The vertical column of these stands terminates in two side-by-side, hollow rectangular blocks made of extremely thin metal that are each about 1.5\\" long, slightly offset from one another. They're about as thick as your pinky finger. Into these blocks, one from each side, you slide T-shaped blocks of also-hollow metal, which are even thinner. On the ends of these two T-shaped blocks, forming the top of the \\"T,\\" are two little L-bracket supports (you can see the upward edges in the product image) that are *literally* two inches in length. That is all the support your monitors have: these little L-shaped supports on the left and right sides, each two inches long, supporting a monitor that is likely about 4-6 times as long as these skinny little supports. After you've inserted these wobbly T-blocks into the center of the larger blocks, you \\"adjust\\" the length of the base by sliding them in as far as you want, and then tightening a hand screw (also visible in image) below to \\"hold\\" the blocks in place. \\"Hold\\" is being generous, considering that these things wobble from side to side no matter how tight you turn the screws. If you rested your monitors, side by side, on the flat side of a wooden 2\\"x4\\", they would be several times as well-balanced and stable than they are on the top of this joke of a product.

To make absolutely sure that you don't buy this, here is a way to visualize what this looks like. Imagine taking two spoons, and placing them side by side, with the spoon ends facing opposite directions, and with about half the length of one handle touching the other handle. Something like this: d...;;;;'''P. Then, imagine taking these side-by-side spoons and taping them to the top of a microphone stand so that the spoons face upwards. Voila! You're done. You can rest your monitor directly on top of the spoons, and have about the same level of stability as that offered by these $70 stands.

I won't even get into the fact that the vertical column is composed of one hollow pipe within another to allow the stand to be raised, which makes the whole stand wobbles around this pivot point too. If you held the stand up an arm's length away and shake it, it wobbles itself to pieces within a few seconds. There are candleholders built more rigidly than this.

Samson, the company producing these stands, should be completely ashamed of itself for knowingly ripping off customers like this. It doesn't take a genius to figure out that even supporting a textbook on this flimsy piece of junk requires a delicate balancing act, so I don't see how they could offer these for sale as \\"studio monitor stands\\" without having absolutely no shame for themselves.

review_headline: defective screw holes, stripped my screws

Obviously I stopped after stripping only a short bit of the screw, but the damage was done.  The seller refused to accept the pickup for a refund.  Instead I was forced to send it back to DiMarzio's factory.  I'm still waiting for them to repair the item.  Meanwhile, my guitar sits, unplayable (no strings) while I wait for this piece of junk to be fixed.

product_title: BEHRINGER B-1
review_headline: the best MIC I've seen ever
review_body:
After setting up my home studio and using this mic with x1204usb mixer i couldnt belive the clearity of this mic, it deserve each penny paid aand more.

this is the best mic I have ever seen or use, it come in small brief case as a set with shock mount and huge black sponge filter.

i found my self writing this review because i can't just pass by a great product such like this without leaving a review.

deserved 5 stars or even 6!!

product_title: Planet Waves Woven Guitar Strap
review_body: The colors are very bright and the pattern is awesome, I got the \\"1\\" version. It's a little rough on the skin but softens up after a while. Try washing with softener.. The plastic seems alittle cheap but if it breaks id bye another haha it's only 8 bucks! (with tax) but if taken care of it shld do just fine. I'd recommend definitely for the price. Good luck :)

product_title: Dunlop 926 Lap Dawg Tonebar, Chromed Brass
review_body: This Slide is really comfortable and provides excellent tonal voicing when used on an acoustic lap guitar.  the weight is just right and fits the hand exactly.

product_title: Electro-Harmonix LPB-1 Linear Power Booster Preamp Pedal
review_body:
Not a lot of frills here, but simple pedals are sometimes the most useful.

I'm the only guitarist in a funk/alt rock band, so I do a lot of back-and-forth from rhythms and chords to lead work. This little guy is invaluable. I have the boost set around 11 o'clock, and it gives a powerful punch for solos, bringing the notes up above the rest of the band.

It doesn't color my tone at all. I have it set right after my tuner and wah, before my OD/fuzz pedals. Seems like it adds just a touch of gain, which is A-OK with me, since I'm usually using some type of distortion/overdrive. Not sure if it's different at another spot in the pedal chain... I know some people keep it at the very end of the chain, which could be a good option if you need a signal boost (for all you guys who use two dozen pedals).

No \\"click\\" when you turn it on... the foot switch is easy, LED light is bright and the boost is powerful. Like I said, I have mine at 11 o'clock... so, there's lots of room to crank it if you really need to get loud.

And for the price, you can't beat it.

product_title: D'Addario EJ34 Folk Nylon Guitar Strings, Ball End, 80/20 Bronze/Black Nylon Trebles
review_body: Good strings.  I had to quickly order so that I could replace the other strings (steel) that I mistakenly put on my classical guitar to replace the old nylon ones -- I ordered \\"folk\\" strings assuming they would be nylon, and it never occurred to me that the strings might be steel or even that the guitar(s) I was using these days was not a \\"folk\\" guitar but a classical one. I still used the strings (never even considering they might harm my instrument).  Someone (an Amazon buyer/peruser)was kind enough to tell me that the metal folk strings would damage my guitar or ruin it. Who knew? I hadn't touched my guitar in such a long time, I guess I lost all common sense knowledge regarding it.  Anyhoo, immediately took off the steel strings (although I did like the folksy twangy sound -- guess I'll just have to get a folk guitar for that).  But these strings have the ball attached making them as easy (almost) at replacing as the steel strings were.  I had my doubts if those balls would hold on the plastic but so far so good.  I started not to review the strings before because I knew I would not be a reliable judge where it mattered most but by reviewing, it helped me avoid a potential huge mistake.  I left the old review on (for the \\"folk\\" strings) in case anyone else was as clueless as I had been.  So take this review with a grain of salt, too. LOL!  Strings seem fine and thanks again to that person who clued me in that steel strings would eventually ruin a classical guitar!

product_title: Dean Stack in the Box: Includes Headphones,and Amplifier
review_headline: Nice way to practice late at night...
review_body: I played this thing all weekend....on the clean setting with my big hollowbody and on the distortion settings on my solid body guitars...it performed great.  I had a Rockman back in the early 80's which allowed me to practice onboard a Navy ship without bothering others and recently my practice schedule changed and I needed a way to practice late at night while my family was asleep...after checking out the price differences, I took a chance on the \\"Stack In A Box\\" ....turns out a wise choice for me.  It's light, easy to use and sounds great....the only drawback that I can tell is the choice of volume settings...the low setting is fine for me most times, but it would be nice to have choices other than just low and high...  Nice item, serves my purpose....and it is dirt cheap for what you get! It even came with a battery!

product_title: Nuts & Bolts Frog Figurine with Guitar
review_body: I received everything in great condition, when expected. Great product. It was for a gift and the recipient was very happy.

product_title: Al Cass Valve Oil, 2.0 fluid Oz.
review_body: Not a pro, just a hobby player and have used different kinds of oil. Al Cass is so much better. I play a Bach Strat 37 and a Yamaha student 232 vintage for fun. Both horns do well with this oil. The Bach works so much better. The Bach oil really didn't cut it but this stuff is like the Slick 50 for the trumpet. Valves are very happy. I can't say enough good about this oil. Yeah, the bottle is a little flimsy but if you're careful with it, no problems should emerge. Remember to keep your horn happy by keeping it clean and slides greased. great oil. Love it.

product_title: Snarks Packs
review_body: The product lights up when turned on, but doesn't react when I strum the strings.  Maybe this is inexpensive for a reason...it is cheap and quality is poor.

product_title: Snark SN-8 Super Tight All Instrument Tuner Packs…
review_body: This is hands-down the best tuner I've *ever* owned. The Snark SN8 works extremely well, and being chromatic, works on every stringed instrument I own (guitar, bass, banjo, violin) no matter what key the instrument is tuned to. I still use my Korg Pitchblack inline with my bass (also a very nice product), but that is mainly to get more cord length across the stage and still keep my signal strong. This little baby is amazingly easy to use, and always accurate. It has a nice bright easy to read display in any lighting situation and makes tuning a breeze and not a hassle (just as it should be - I've personally always hated those Boss pedal tuners). It simply does its job and does it very well.  Also, buying this item from Amazon saved me quite a bit over the local Guitar Center, which is always a big plus. It feels tough too, this thing feels like it can easily handle the rigors of being tossed around, which is a very good thing. Despite the flimsy way the seller packaged this for shipping, the product arrived intact, and fast. I would have cropped a star for a damaged product in that little wimpy envelope they sent it in. Fortunately mine arrived in perfect condition (no thanks to that paper envelope - seriously, they should use a stiff cardboard envelope or small tube or something).  I could not be happier, at least until I buy another one to keep at the house while the first stays in my gig bag.

product_title: Protec Guitar Strap featuring Thick Leather Ends and Pick Pocket, Black
review_headline: It's a strap, what else do you want?
review_body:
For less than six dollars you can't even buy a hamburger meal. To get a strap for the guitar seems like this is a good price as long as it works.

The material is durable and it's a simple guitar strap that works. Enough said. If you want leather, pay the money. But don't complain you got something made in China and that isn't leather for less than six dollars. Use some common sense. Save your, not for China money for the guitar instead. Some things are better made in China.

product_title: Dunlop NC65  Formula 65 Neck Cradle Maintenance Station
review_body: The Dunlop neck cradle is well designed and firmly supports the neck of any guitar. It is self adjusting and makes restringing a breeze!  Buy one, and I am sure you will like it as well as I.

product_title: Alesis SR16 | Classic 24-bit Stereo Electronic Drum Machine with Dynamic Articulation
review_body:
I bought one of these several years ago. The last time I tried to hook it up, and powered up, and everything looked normal. However, upon connecting the cables to an amp, no sound was produced.

I was talking to my friend last night about wanting to buy a drum machine, and without mentioning my experience or Alesis by name, he brought up an Alesis SR-16 that he had - but it doesn't output sound.

These things WILL stop working. Google it.

product_title: DW Drum Workshop 8000 Series Bass Drum Pedal
review_body:
This is one of the three pedals I routinely use. My favorite is the [[ASIN:B0002II8A4 Ludwig Speed King Single Bass Drum Pedal]] and the other is the [[ASIN:B0002EKG6W Pearl P2000B Eliminator Single Bass Drum Pedal, Belt Drive]].

What I love about this DW model, though, is it pretty much works out of the box and is reliable. I expect it to last a lifetime. Regarding working out of the box, it seemed to be perfectly adjusted for my personal playing style without any tweaking (other than adjusting the spring tension to my preference.) No fuss and no muss.

I am not a speed player and play heel down, so folks who stomp on pedals may have a different experience and set of opinions. I am a firm believer in trying pedals in person before making a purchase decision because, like drum sticks, the feel is so personal and each person is so different that buying without trying can lead to disappointment.

This may sound silly, but aside from this pedal doing what it's supposed to and being built like a tank I love the built-in drum key holder on the floorboard. I wish more pedals came that way because it is one feature that has come in handy time and again.

If you want a meat and potatoes pedal, and especially if you are playing lighter music, this model is worth checking out.

product_title: DBX 376 Tube Preamp Channel Strip with Digital Out
review_headline: Thanks for sending a new cable!
review_body: Aww thanks so much for the cable! :)  You guys are great and the preamp works perfect! I love it!

product_title: Elite Core OSP DL-320 Dynamic Vocal Microphone
review_body:
I have a couple of these OSP DL-320s AND I have a Shure SM-58 as well. I'm not an 'audiophile' type, but I can't hear any difference between the Shure and the OSP. They are virtually identical in every way (though I should mention the parts are not interchangable).

I have a home rehearsal studio and I'm on a pretty tight budget so I bought a couple of the OSP DL-320 mics for the same price as a single Shure SM-58. I'm 100% satisfied with them. They're durable, sound great and even look like the Shure. I also bought a couple OSP DL-330 mics (Shure SM-57 clones) and I'm just as happy with those too.

product_title: M-Audio SP Electronic Keyboard Pedal or Footswitch
review_body: Arrived on time and in excellent condition.  Does not provide quite the sustain quality I was used to with my baby grand, but probably as good as it gets for a keyboard.  Easy to set up - I was using it within 5 minutes of unwrapping the box.  Easy to position for comfort.

product_title: Snark SN-2 All Instrument Clip-On Chromatic Tuner
review_headline: Great tuner! Could have a slightly larger jaw.
review_body: On my cello this tuner barely spans the headstock thickness. But it's a fantastic tuner, very accurate, with a beautiful, brilliant, intelligent display. Others have enumerated the features. The manual could have been a tad more informative, but I figured it out on my own eventually.

product_title: BEHRINGER PB1000
review_body: This product is not durable. I would recommend purchasing a smaller brand or model of this pedal board. 6 slots would work much better than this one. I have never not liked my other behringer products... This was a surprise.

product_title: Chauvet DJ LX-5 Moonflower LED Light
review_body:
This is a great light for the price. It has no moving parts and it is an LED light so used very little power and it don't get hot. It has no duty cycle so you can leave it on all night.
There are YouTube videos you can watch too. It puts out colored dots that flash and appear to move because different ones go on and off. The farther its away from the wall or floor the bigger the pattern is. Its all metal with a bracket and you can choose the sound active mode or patterns. This light is great to add some color and fun and for smaller light shows.

product_title: Fender Classic Series '72 Telecaster Thinline Electric Guitar,
review_body:
I've owned this guitar for about 7 years and will never get rid of it. In the past 3 months alone I've had 3 people offer to purchase it from me. I loaned it to a friend to play and he had a random person from the crowd try to buy it off of him after the show!

This is not your typical Tele. It comes with humbuckers so its much warmer. Please play it in a store before you purchase it. I used to play it through a Mesa Boogie and now I play it through a Fender Deville 4x10. If you want to rock, this guitar is for you. If you want to play blues, this guitar is for you, and if you want amazing clean tone this guitar is for you.

I play this guitar more than any other guitar I own (I have 7), including my Gibson Les Paul Standard which was twice the cost! Don't get me wrong, Les Pauls are incredible, however, if you are going to spend around $500 to $800 you really cannot find a better sound than the 72 Thinline Tele. Even with humbuckers it still has that classic Fender twang when you crank up the tone (not as mid heavy as the les pauls).

This is why Amazon allows you to rate something 5 stars, because 4 is simply not enough.

product_title: Suzuki Promaster Hammond Harmonica
review_body: Well, made, sounds great. Can't go wrong with this one. Definately one of my favorite instruments. Nothing Suzuki ever seems to be badly put together.

product_title: Bach 1877 Trumpet Repair/Maintenance Kit
review_body: I bought this kit to revive my Bach trumpet that had been sitting in the closet for years.  Everything you need and then some is in this kit.  Just what the doctor ordered!

product_title: Lanikai LU-21B Baritone Ukulele
review_body: I had to import this into South Africa as non of the local retailers were selling any baritone ukes.  I find it hard to buy a musical instrument without first playing it but took a chance on the Lanikai and I'm glad I did.  Plays beautifully, sounds great. I really love my new friend Bari.

product_title: Planet Waves Pro-Winder String Winder and Cutter
review_headline: Planet Waves Pro Winder String Winder and Cutter
review_body: I am a tightwad and don't buy things I don't need. I bought my son and I each a Snark Tuner and needed something else to qualify for free shipping. I've seen this winder before and thought \\"cool but I already have a winder and side snips in my case\\" but this was cheap and was just enough for the free shipping. OK THIS is a GREAT tool!!! I thought it would be cheap and gimmicky but was surprised to find that it's really well built. Cutter works well even on light ga. unwound strings. Well done Planet Waves!!!

product_title: Whirlwind EDB1
review_body: No issues at all.  Clean DI and cheaper than a lot of others.  All of the standard options including ground lift and pad.

product_title: Cooperstand Ecco-G Guitar Stand
review_body:
I had purchased 4 of the wood version of this guitar stand. They are great looking but a bit delicate and my husband is a tad bit rough on things. I would not recommend using the wood version for performances on stage. BUT the Ecco-G stand are super!!

Great design, small footprint, fits in the guitar case. Which is great as it's that much less to haul to a gig as it's in the case and ready for use. Plus it looks great and really showcases the guitars nicely. Very secure, the center of gravity prevents them from falling over it accidentally bumped.

I would also like to add that I originally came across the wood version at the Woodstock Luthiers show and both my husband and I were immediately sold on the product. Cooperstand is a great company to deal with direct as well.

product_title: Kelly Mouthpieces Small Shank Trombone 6-1/2AL Mouthpiece Crystal Green
review_body: My son loves his kelly mouthpiece, it came promptly and well packed with zero issues. He has been using it every day since Christmas and it is his one of his schools colors.

product_title: FiiO D3 Digital to Analog Audio Converter - 192kHz/24bit Optical and Coaxial DAC
review_headline: Analog sounds for our Samsung PN59D7000!
review_body: We just purchased a [[ASIN:B004MN79A0 Samsung PN59D7000]] and we wanted to hook it up to our [[ASIN:B000FHA7E2 Yamaha RX-497 Receiver]].  We are so happy that this product is available because it's the cheapest solution to getting sounds through the loudspeakers.  There are other products similar to this, but I don't know if they are as simple to use - they're definitely not as cheap.  We also purchased an [[ASIN:B001TH7GSW AmazonBasics Digital Optical Audio Toslink Cable]], which we plugged into the \\"Digital Audio Out (Optical)\\" port on the TV and the other end into the \\"Optical In\\" on the FiiO D3.  We have an extra red-white-yellow cable, so we're using the red and white plugs to connect from the FiiO to the receiver.  We plugged in the power, turned the receiver to the proper channel and there was only noise, so we changed the audio format on the TV from Digital Dolby to PCM, and that was it!  If you recently purchased a new TV with only an optical out, and you don't want to spend at least another $200 on a new receiver for an optical in, you can buy this and an optical audio cable; you'll be as happy as we are about this little black box.

product_title: Kun Original 1/4 Violin Shoulder Rest
review_body: My son has been using it since November 2011 ... So far so good ... It still works like it should.

product_title: Pearl T2000 Tom Stand with TH-2000S
review_body: I reduced the number of toms from 5 to 2. Then my 3 elements Pearl rack looked ugly and useless. With 3 double stands, i can have 4 cymbals and 2toms. Or 3 toms and 3 cymbals. review_body: Over-all I'm satisfied with the keyboard bag. review_body: It is a great product for those starting out but, I immediately realized that I was going to have to upgrade to something more costly and complex if i wanted to get serious about this and if i wanted it to be my career. But, great product for the casual Dj.

product_title: Mighty Bright Triple LED Music Stand Light, with Bag

product_title: Kurzweil PC361 61 Note Synthesizer Action Performance Controller and V.A.S.T. Workstation Keyboard, Lightly Weighted Keys, Black
review_body: Back oh so many years ago, I bought a Kurzweil K2000.  Since then I've been through Roland, Yamaha & Korg workstations and found them all lacking.  I kept thinking the pretty, bigger screens, the onboard audio tracks and all the other bells an whistles they had would help me create a smoother, more organic workflow.  They each proved quite the opposite for me.  Learning the ins & outs of all of the Big 3's flagship workstations was like learning a 3 new languages.  After a while, I remember saying (with each one) \\"I just want to jot down a quick idea...\\"  but getting that idea into the internal sequencer was just too convoluted and made me feel like I was a computer programmer 1st and a songwriter 2nd.  Each of the Big 3 had me feeling that way and I was just about to give up and go entirely software based when I saw that the PC361 was only around $1300.    So I popped into a nearby Guitar Center where they had a PC3 in their used section.  I made them plug it in & hook it up.  Within 30 seconds I had a fun little ditty in the sequencer.  I then noticed how many buttons and sliders have been added since the K2000 days and thought at $1300 I'll give Kurzweil another go.  I am very happy I did.   Yeah, it doesn't have the big color screen but that keeps it from being too confusing.  And to be honest, if you do your research you'll find the the PC3 is much, much, much deeper than any of the big 3 flagship workstations.  But only if you want to go that deep.    I went back & forth with spending the extra grand (!) to get the PC3K6 so I could load some of my old K2000 samples into it, but I opted for the PC361 and don't regret my decision.  It does more than enough and if I feel I need the sampling option I'll reconsider.    In the meantime, thank you Kurzweil for sticking to such a great product.  Instead of scrapping the whole (amazing) V.A.S.T. architecture for something 'flashier', you do what most of us wish the others would do - Improve the great product you already have.  Keep it up.

product_title: Hosa Inch Right Angle9
review_body: A great cable. With strong clear sound at a great price. Only thing I did not like is that the joints have a plastic tape wrap instead of a spring system which I prefer and which tends to last a longer time since even if it gets bent it does not crack. Nor does the spring system wear out at the point where the connector makes contact with the wire.

product_title: Espana Classical Guitar w/Hardshell Case
review_body: After I decided that I wanted to get a classical guitar, I spent quite a bit of time reviewing the different models in the $200-$500 range.  After much deliberation, I decided to try the Dean.  The reviews I read about it here and elsewhere clinched the deal.  I have owned several electric guitars and a steel string acoustic over the years, but this was my first nylon-stringed guitar.  I have to say that I was amazed!  This is a quality guitar for a very reasonable price.  The hard shell case alone makes it worth it, but the sound is great as well.  Deep bass and nice highs compliment this guitar very much.  For the beginner, this is a perfect way to start.  My advice to someone just starting out in any endeavor is to start at the lower price spectrum and work your way up.  Don't buy a thousand dollar guitar that you can't possibly get the most out of unless you've just won the lottery.  Guitars like this Dean will keep you interested as you start your journey.  Once you've gotten all you can out of it, then it's time for an upgrade.

product_title: Clarke Pennywhistle in Key of D
review_body: I previously had a penny whistle and gave up on it a little too quickly and discarded it. The idea of a wooden fipple on this Clarke penny whistle made it very appealing, but the sound does not come out nearly as clearly as it did with the plastic fipple. I read so many positive reviews about this penny whistle that I thought I would give it a try. I was also under the impression that the fipple would actually be a wooden mouth piece, but it is metal with a wood block inside. Perhaps it was my misunderstanding, but a bit of a disappointment nonetheless. Anyway, it does play okay, and maybe for a more advanced player it is much better. I hope that this review helps you. Good luck!

product_title: Mendini 1/2 MV Solid Wood Violin with Hard Case, Shoulder Rest, Bow, Rosin and Extra Strings
review_body: I bought this violin from the same company (KK), but on another site (ebay). Except they included an electric tuner for 5 dollars extra. First off the package that it was delivered in had a huge chunk ripped out of it, probably from UPS. The violin case itself was left unscathed luckily. It came in a black zippered case, with a nice little flap to hide the zipper tabs. I wasn't expecting a nice package from a cheap product, but when I opened it, it impressed me. Nice little compartment for strings and rosin, and a strap to hold the violin in place and another strap for the bow. It had a nice little faux-velvet interior and there was a cut-out velvet strip to place over the violin when not in use.  First thing, you're going to have a long set-up session when you get it. I read the reviews and I figured the bad reviews were from people who did not have a clue or enough initiative to figure out how to set it up. Do yourself a favor and buy an extra rosin and some tuner peg oil. My rosin came crumbled up,I went against going through the hassle of sending it back and went to a local music store and dishing out 5 for a rosin. I noticed that people had problems with the tuning pegs as well. I just applied a dash of silicone lube on the tab, and the tuner tab turned smoothly (even though I'm sure you're not supposed to use lube, but peg oil instead).   The tuning tabs on top are just to tighten the strings, be careful, they will snap easily. When you tune your violin, use the fine tuners at the bottom instead of the large tuners at the top. When you use your rosin it will take about 5 minutes of rubbing the bow on it for it to be properly rosined. Do it in 5-6 increments vigorously, and once your done use long strokes.   I haven't learned to fully use the violin to hear it, but I'll write back on the sound quality.

product_title: CNB PDC-410F Locking Aluminum Pedal Case, Large
review_body: This Pedal case was better then what i expected. Its pretty big, and it comes with two keys. (Durable and secure)

product_title: Gibraltar Extended Height Snare Stand
review_body: It locks down solid, it's heavy duty enough to take a beating from me (and I can be pretty heavy handed), and it let's me get my snare to the front of the stage with everyone else when necessary. It raises to a comfortable level (and beyond) and still goes low enough I can sit down with it. I'm very happy with it.

product_title: Carrion Economy Guitar Case
review_body: Our son decided to take guitar lessons at school, so, bought him a new guitar that came with a soft case.......week 2, guitar busted up.  So, he got a used Fender Acoustic for a replacement, however, was not going to leave this one vunerable, and after reading other reviews, bought this case.  Glad I did.  This case is SOLID, nicely lined, contains a compartment for a tuner, picks, etc. and latches in 4 places.  Keep in mind, I am not a musician (but a true music lover) and find this case exceeds all expectations at this price point.  Others commented on a smell?  not sure what that was as the one received by us does not have that characteristic.  You cannot go wrong with this case at this price!

product_title: Fender Standard Fretless Jazz Bass Guitar,
review_body:
I wanted a fretless that wouldn't break the bank and this one did the trick. Took a couple of tries from my local store (the first one I got had a twisted neck that my tech wouldn't touch) but I wound up with a nice one that didn't require much tweaking to become ready to play.

Be sure to examine the neck and electronics carefully upon receipt. I'll probably swap out the pickups and pots on mine eventually and I'm already tired of the plain pick guard but those are easy mods that can be done any time. They're lots of fun to play when they're set up properly and the quality of the stock pickups may surprise you.

product_title: On-Stage  Studio Monitor Stand
review_headline: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly
review_body: Overall, the product is good for the price I paid.  Briefly here is the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly:  The Good:  The stands are sturdy, easy to set up, and steady when positioned.  I have a pair of Yamaha HS80Ms up on them, and all is well.  Even with the issues I describe below, they are still a pretty good value, but you may want to go up a notch to get around the issues I experienced.  The Bad:  Like other reviewers, the plastic cable clips were shattered into a dozen little pieces when the stands arrived.  I can live with that, because they were so fragile, I'd expect them to break shortly after arrival if they had not been DOA, and would like more cable control anyway.  The more frustrating issue was the threads for the carpet spikes.  Most were OK, but I could not get 2 of the spikes to thread properly into one of the stands.  I finally got them going, but suspect they are cross threaded.  If only one were messed up, it would be no big deal to get the stand plumb, but with two messed up on the same stand, getting the stands plumb and the monitors level is a chore.  Disappointing.  The Ugly:  For the most part, I like the way the stands look, but the adhesive graphics were pretty beat up and ragged looking when the stands arrived.  This has no functional impact, but does take away from the aesthetics.  If you like everything in your control room crisp, clean, and new looking, you may not get it with these stands.

product_title: Shredneck Dreadneck Natural
review_body: This little piece of equipment is amazing! I received it in the mail today and I can't set it down. I bought it for when I travel or for when lying in bed (so I don't bother my wife). It is the perfect size, very sturdy construction, and very appealing to the eyes. The only thing that would have made this better is if they included a built in battery and headphone jack so that you could hear what you were playing. However, even without that feature it still makes a great tool to practice chords, scales, and for warming up. I highly recommend! I bought the Acoustic version and it definitely has an acoustic feel.

product_title: KRK KNS-8400 Studio Headphones
review_headline: KRK KNS8400 vs Bose AE2 Headphones
review_body:
This is an easy review for me to write, both headphones KRK KNS8400 and the Bose AE2 sound exactly the same, there is no difference whatsoever as sound quality is concerned. Oddly enough the Bose is much better at isolating external noise. The KRK does not a good job in this regard at all. The KRK work more like open headphones. The KRK comes with a volume control in the box, at least the one I bought did.
I returned this KRK headphones because despite been very comfortable they are not nearly as comfortable and light as the Bose which you can keep on your head for hours , the Bose AE2 is light as a feather. product_title: Fender Texas Special Solderless Stratocaster Pickups 3
review_headline: Has a bark and a bite!
review_body:
I've used lots of P-Bass pickups. I preferred the single coil first generation Precision until I tried this pickup in a Mexican P-Bass I bought. It sounded good before, but when I put this pickup in it the bass sounded much brighter and more alive. It is now my favorite gigging bass. This pickup has enough lows to get the job done like you'd expect with any P-Bass pickup but the big news here without a doubt is the punchy upper mids that so much reminds me of the bite of a single coil. This is the same pickup used in the '62 American Vintage Reissue Precision, which is a very premium USA bass.

This pickup comes with the brass shielding base plate and the weatherstripping foam already installed.

As already pointed out, this pickup gives your tone control something to do for a change!

Speaking of tone, a tone capacitor change from the standard 0.05 to 0.1uf was done on the '62 RI design to handle the brightness, however if you like the punchy tone there is no real need to change it and it is electrifying to say the least with the 0.05 cap that you find in about any other Fender passive Precision Bass. It sounds darn near active! I'm thinking maybe of trying something in between like a 0.068uf just to mellow it out a bit while still retaining some bark. You won't believe the upper mids or the output this pickup delivers.

A really simple install and a recommended upgrade, especially for Mexican made Fender P-Basses. This is a hotter yet much more versatile pickup than the Seymour Duncan SPB-3 \\"Quarter Pounder\\" that is so popular and yet it is about the same price. This to me is the better buy and I've used both.

The only thing I would not use this for is a P/J bass. I would not suggest using this in a P/J bass because it is so hot that it will totally dominate the Jazz pickup and you'll never hear the Jazz pickup at all.

review_headline: An affordable gem - professional quality at student prices - in simulated Rosewood finish
review_body:
This recorder uses the Baroque (not German) Fingering convention widely used in most countries esp the commonwealth.

+: Produces beautiful warm sonorous tones ... reliable intonation and highly responsive - a joy to play ++ much more.
Easy to maintain - washable. Durable. High standards of manufacture guarantee consistent homogeneous quality between each instrument - you can be confident what
you are purchasing. Selection becomes a non issue. Losses can be replaced by simply purchasing another one and you will know that you will be purchasing similar
performance capability. Professional quality made affordable to the masses.

-: Does clog somewhat after extended play but the instrument can be prepped beforehand with anti-clog solution available from recorder specialist. This was provided
to me when I purchased the YRT 304B but I haven't used it yet.

I am very happy with my purchase of the Yamaha YRS, YRA 314B and 316B (yes I purchased all four) which I think is at par with branded wooden recorders 6-10 times the price. A great second instrument or spare for travelling.

I can personally attest that it is true that the simulated woodgrain finish versions YRA 314 & 316 (strangely enough) produce a superior tone to the normal ABS resin finish 302 model - perhaps this is due to the outer coating that resonates better. For not a lot more, the simulated wood-grain version IS well-worth paying for.

YRA 312B in simulated Rosewood has a rich warm reddish brown colour whilst YRA 314B in simulated Ebony is a quieter yellow brown - both with attractive printed woodgrain finish.

Yamaha did a real service to the world by making this attractive gem so affordable.

product_title: MIDI Solutions Footswitch Controller
review_headline: Pricey, but nothing else does the trick.
review_body:
I'm a professional musician. I've been using this for years with my Yamaha keyboard. My keyboard only has two programmable footswitch inputs. I wanted a third pedal so I could use the MIDI Solutions unit for sustain and the other two for other stuff.

I like that the unit does not operate on batteries but rather the MIDI power of your MIDI instrument.

I can find no other product on the market that does this.

I'm writing this review because I've been using the product for six years, and after six years, it petered out on me. No light switch came on when the unit was plugged into the keyboard.

I brought it to my local music tech who fixes professional gear. To my surprise, they told me that this unit couldn't be fixed because it needed a proprietary chip that's only made by the manufacturer. I started rethinking a little my judgement that this is a simple piece of electronics that is overpriced because the company has a monopoly as no one else makes anything similar.

I emailed MIDI Solutions and offered to pay for repair and shipping. John said that he would take a look at my unit. I shipped it without a tracking #. John fixed it, PROGRAMMED IT for sustain, and shipped it back to me free of charge. Let me repeat, I had let MIDI Solutions know that my controller was six years old!

Of course, I cannot guarantee you this kind of service should yours break, but I think six years of professional use without breaking is a good track record.

product_title: Pyle-Pro PPSS50 50' Foot Professional Speaker Cable Male Compatible With Speakon Connector to Male Compatible With Speakon Connector
review_body: I ordered 2 of these to connect my 15" Subs to my Peavey GPS 2600 and they eventually did the job just fine but I had to exchange one that was DOA and later the second one stopped working, I decided to take it apart to fix it, as I didn't have time to wait for another one to be shipped. I found the ends of the wire had corroded off inside the connector so I had to cut, and re strip the wire to repair it, this is also when I notice that the cable is not 12 AWG (gauge) maybe closer to a small 14 AWG. However, they have worked nicely ever since I repaid them so I guess It's not a real big deal as I am only pushing 600W RMS through them. A photo comparing the cable to a true 14AWG cable is attached to the product page. If Pyle stepped up QC on the cable and corrected the false Gauge Advertising this would be a 5 star product.  Edit: I used these cables for several years before I upgraded my system with an 18" 1600W sub with a 4Ohm Voice coil. With the upgrade in power and lower impedance I wouldn't suggest these cables, I ended up moving the speakon style ends to a true 14/2 cable I bought (the one pictured) and I put 1/4" Mono Radioshack plugs on the Pyle cable and use it for my mains (about 150W RMS and 8Ohm Impedance) and it works decently for that. While I had it apart I measured the resistance on the wire at 0.3 Ohms for 1 run of the 15' (double that for the total cable resistance of 0.6 Ohms) this equates to approximately 20 Ohms per 1000' which means this cable is equivalent to about 23 AWG in copper, so nowhere near the 12AWG they claim.

product_title: Ibanez V70ce Acoustic-Electric Guitar Black
review_headline: Good guitar, great value, but not a top end instrument.
review_body:
I gave this guitar 4 stars because considering the price, it's a good product. However, if you're a serious guitarist looking for a serious instrument, you may want to spend more. The neck has good action which makes it easy to play and the built in pickup sounds good. Not amazing, but it has a full sound, better than some other guitars in this price range. Unplugged, it sounds ok, but it really lacks the tone and volume of the more expensive models. This guitar works best when plugged in.

The tuners are high quality and hold tune well, and the black finish looks nice but scratches can be easily seen on it. The guitar's not very heavy, which makes it feel a little fragile. I don't feel like it's built to last. The biggest drawback is the lack of a built-in tuner, this is a big issue for playing live shows. If you're going to tune you have to unplug from the PA and plug into a tuner, or buy a pedal tuner and leave it plugged in. Or tune by ear, which the audience does not want to hear. If you have a pedal tuner or are not planning to perform live shows, it's not an issue.

Overall I'd recommend this guitar to the aspiring player as a starter, or for the casual guitarist who jams with friends and does the occasional open mic night, but if you have any more serious ambitions, buy something a little better.

product_title: MXL 770 Cardioid Condenser Microphone
review_body: I bought this mic about 3 months ago and have since had the chance to try it out on a lot of different projects.  Acoustic guitars and vocals came out clear and rich sounding.  Then I used it for recording distorted electric guitars, and I wasn't as impressed, but it got the job done (leads sounded pretty good, but chords and muting came out kind of muddled - definitely a job more suited for a Shure SM-57).  One of the things that pushed me toward this mic was reading up on it on the MXL website, which very clearly states what each mic should be used for (it does not list electric guitars for this mic).  It said this one could be used for drums, and right now, I'm only using an MBox (2 channel interface), so I needed a mic that could capture everything on the set, with the kick mic'd separately.  I wouldn't rely on this method for high quality punk or metal recordings as the cymbals will likely drown everything out, but I was using it for reggae and more mellow jazzy stuff, and it worked awesomely.  The -10dB switch is a good feature for keeping the levels in the right range for louder recording (electric guitars and drums). Other things that make this mic totally worth it are the shock mount, case, and the design/color.  Well, the case is plastic and cheap-looking, but I knew I would be traveling with this thing, so I needed a case, and assuming the case doesn't break, it will keep my mic safe.  For the money, this mic is totally worth it; and someday when money isn't an issue, I'll definitely keep this on hand for drum overheads and acoustic/vocal work.  If you're new to condenser mics, make sure you have phantom power, whether it's on your recording device or separate.

product_title: Saga LC-10 Deluxe Electric Guitar Kit - Single Cutaway
review_headline: Nice woodwork, shame about the rest
review_body: I bought this after helping build a telecaster kit for my nephew.  I liked the idea of a custom made guitar that looked quite like a Paul Reed Smith, rather than the bog standard Strat or Telecaster.  The finish on the body and neck was lovely, so I decided to go with light tinted lacquer on the body and just oiled the neck to keep the smoothness.  This would allow the grain and sublte striping to show through, assuming I could do it correctly.  That was the plan, anyway.  As it turns out I'm useless at woodwork and lacquering, but still got it to look reasonably like I had planned.  Varnish and lacquer took many days with many rounds of coating and drying, so dont think you'll build this thing in minutes.  Assembly takes minutes in comparison, you are just screwing and hammering the stuff together.  Rather than go with the cheap silver hardware that comes with it, I spent cash buying better quality gold hardware.  It was more for looks, but you really must change the cheap & nasty tuning pegs for good quality ones, otherwise you'll never stay in tune.  The BIG downside with this kit is the electronics and wiring.  The wiring harness as supplied is worse than useless.  The cheaper kit I built was exactly the same, the wiring appeared to be wired in a completely random way, almost like a film prop so it looks like a guitar but doesn't work.  Bizarre.  I found a diagram on the internet for wiring 2 humbucker setups, and it works a treat when rewired correctly.  The volume & tone pots are made of some very soft metal and even just fitting the knobs on them buckled them.  Garbage.  The actual pickups themselves are alright, but you might want to replace them anyway when replacing everything else.  In short, this is a lovely looking bit of woodwork with rotten electrics.  You should buy the kit, and at the same time buy new tuning pegs, pots, pickups and some solder.  I wish I was better at woodwork and lacquering, but its passable and looks fab at a distance.  Last thing I did was spend 10 bucks buying new fret marker stickers from Japan.  There's a company there that makes superb inlay stickers that transform the look of the neck, and I bought a set of flying bird ones so it completes the PRS look.

review_body: Like the diff colors to let you know when you're on-tune. Light & easy to handle but - not deep enough groove in back to open battery slot and has to be placed just right. It's better than most tuners tho.

review_body: This item is exactly what was need for my Yamaha keyboard.  Have used keyboard for many years but never realized it could be set up with this sustain pedal.  Wow!  What an improvement.  Works great!

review_body: I couldn't be happier with this guitar. It's beautiful and sounds fantastic. It's the best in it's class in every detail. Tunes easily and stays in tune. I couldn't ask for any more in this price range. There's no question that Epiphone makes a quality guitar. I'm very satisfied.

product_title: Akai Professional MPK Mini 25-Key Ultra-Portable USB MIDI Keyboard Controller (OLD MODEL)
review_body: Purchased this item to use as a midi controller.  Have had many keyboards over the years but this is my first USB midi controller.  All the functions work well and it works with my software.  I am very disappointed with the keys; both of the keyboard and the pads.  The keys are very stiff and required a lot of force to get them to play.  I am a very large man and have big, heavy hands and it makes my hands tired having to press the keys hard enough to get the required sound.  They are touch sensitive keys but should to be a lot easier to press and use.  As for the pads, forget about it.  Have to hit them really, really hard to get sound out of them.  Lights work etc but they are too stiff also.  I've had keyboards that included pads, years ago, that you could play with pencils.  This one would need the handle end of a screw driver to get them to play.  Even hitting them very hard, with heavy fingers, you still can't get dependable response from the pads.  The keyboard is very small(keys are a bit too small)and easy to carry and seems to have good build quality but if it's too hard to play it isn't worth having.  This one is going back for a refund and I'll buy another midi controller. I would have rated it a one but it does have a few workable features other than the stiff key issues.

review_body: I just bought a used Fender Passport 150 for $199.  I bought this portable PA because I was tired of lugging huge speakers and a big mixer for solo acoustic gigs. product_title: Cremona Premier Novice Violin
review_headline: Cremona SV-75 Premier Novice Violin, 1/8 Size
review_body: This nice Cremona SV-75 Premier Novice Violin, 1/8 Size, is hand-carved in solid Spruce and its top, neck, back and sides are hand-carved in solid Maple. The purfling is painted and its finish is a warm brown finish, exactly as shown on the picture. It also has dyed Rosewood fingerboard and fittings, as well as dyed hardwood chinrest VP-61 tailpiece with 4 built-in fine tuners.   It comes in a beautiful featherweight arched-top shaped hard case with blue exterior and light grey velvet interior. On the outside, there is a pocket to store music sheets (if you fold them) or house keys, nothing too bulky but very practical.   Inside the case, you will find a VP-71 bow: wood stick rosewood frog and unbleached horsehair C-3907.   Strings have a limited lifetime. Apart from obvious things, such as the winding of a string coming undone from wear, players generally change a string when it no longer plays true, losing the desired tone. String longevity depends on string quality and playing intensity. You are provided with those on the violin, but no extra strings.  You also have Rosin provided. Players of bowed string instruments rub cakes or blocks of rosin on their bow hair so it can grip the strings and make them speak. Lighter rosin is used for violins, darker for cellos, special type for basses. Violin rosin can be applied to the underside of bridges in other musical instruments, such as the Banjo and Banjolele, in order to prevent the bridge from moving during vigorous playing.  The violon is exactly as shown on the picture, every piece is where it is supposed to be. The only exception is that you have to install the bridge yourself (and it is like that to make sure that nothing will be broken during the shipping process) and tune it afterwards.  Product Dimensions: 17 x 6 x 2.8 inches  Shipping Weight: 8.8 ounces  ASIN: B0026IC6XI   Item model number: SV-75 1/8   Children typically use smaller string instruments than adults. Violins are made in so-called fractional sizes for young students: Apart from full-size (4/4) violins, 3/4, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/10, 1/16, 1/32 and even 1/64-sized instruments exist, although these smaller sizes are highly unusual and usually custom-made. Extremely small sizes were developed, along with the Suzuki program, for violin students as young as 3. Finely made fractional sized violins, especially smaller than 1/2 size, are extremely rare or non-existent.    These fractional sizes have nothing to do with the actual dimensions of an instrument; in other words, a 3/4-sized instrument is not three-quarters the length of a full size instrument. The body length (not including the neck) of a full-size, or 4/4, violin is about 14 inches (35 cm), smaller in some 17th century models. A 3/4 violin is about 13 inches (33 cm), and a 1/2 size is approximately 12 inches (30 cm). With the violin's closest family member, the viola, size is specified as body length in inches or centimeters rather than fractional sizes. A full-size viola averages 16 inches (40 cm).  Occasionally, an adult with a small frame may use a so-called 7/8 size violin instead of a full-size instrument. Sometimes called a lady's violin, these instruments are slightly shorter than a full size violin, but tend to be high-quality instruments capable of producing a sound that is comparable to that of fine full size violins.  THIS VIOLIN IS PERFECT FOR A YOUNG CHILD WANTING TO START LEARNING, WHO IS STILL GROWING FAST AND WILL HAVE TO CHANGE SIZE IN A MATTER OF 6, 12 OR 18 MONTHS. I AM QUITE SATISFIED WITH THIS VIOLIN OF A SOMEWHAT LOWER QUALITY. IT IS PERFECT FOR BEGINNERS NEEDING A RUGGED VIOLIN, AND WHOSE RUDIMENTARY TECHNIQUE DOES NOT JUSTIFY THE EXPENSE OF A MORE CAREFULLY MADE ONE (SINCE YOU NEED SOME TIME TO SEE IF THE STUDENT WILL WANT TO CONTINUE PLAYING, LIKES IT, ETC.) AT WHICH TIME, ONCE THE CHILD HAS FULLY GROWN, YOU INVEST IN A FULL SIZE EXCELLENT QUALITY ONE.  I RECOMMEND THIS VIOLIN TO ALL PARENTS WHO HAVE A SMALLER BUDGET BUT WANT TO PROVIDE THEIR CHILD WITH THE GIFT OF LEARNING MUSIC.

product_title: Ibanez Arz307 7-String Electric Guitar Black
review_body:
I went to my local guitar center and honestly I've never played a 7-string before today but I thought id give it a try today and OH MY GOSHNESS! IT FELT SSOOO nice. I mean im used to a 6 string so at first it felt weird and looking at the strings was confusing but then I started playing around with it a bit more and I completely LOVE this guitar.. if I had 500 dollars id make this mine.. so if you have 500 dollars I very thoroughly suggest you buy this guitar! its fast, it feels ssooo great in the hand, and that last lower sounding string is just amazing. not to mention how just totally breath taking this guitar looks. if you dont believe me go try it out somewhere. you wont regret it.

product_title: Behringer Ultravoice Xm8500 Dynamic Vocal Microphone, Cardioid
review_body: I bought this microphone back in January. It's June now, almost July, and it's still fully functional and works like a charm. I purchased this along with a [[ASIN:B001EW5YQS Blue Microphones Icicle XLR to USB Mic Converter/Mic Preamp]]. I do a weekly podcast over Skype, and it sounds fantastic. The noise cancellation is such that I can have my microphone right next to my computer's speakers, and most of the time I do, and there's no echo, no feedback. It's just a cool, crisp sound. I definitely recommend this if you're looking to do broadcasting out of your bedroom as I do. I can't really speak on the microphone's effectiveness for recording vocals though.

product_title: Heritage Edition Tube Microphone 4
review_headline: EDIT: Not the best sound for altos - HOWEVER - the best mic for the price
review_body: I am saddened by the fact that I didn't bother reading any reviews from female vocalists before buying this, because it could've saved me some money.  This is a great mic for the price, there is no doubt - it is crisp, clear and quite a surprising find for its cost.  However, when I used it it simply did not work with my voice. I'm not sure what about it is the problem, but compared to an AT2020 (which doesn't sound as high quality unfortunately), female vocals tend to sound a bit weaker than usual.  EDIT: After buying the RODE NT1A and the AT3035 - I have to edit my review and say that, hands down, this is THE BEST mic you can buy for its price. It just blows everything else out of the water. It might not sound the very best on my voice (female alto) - but the quality of sound it produces does make up for it.  So after a few years, I'm going to throw in another star. It deserves better.  This is definitely something you should try before buying if you're a female vocalist!

product_title: Musicmaide MMAZ1000 Wind Clips for music stand (Pair)
review_body: We use 8 of these clips for our outdoor string quartet wedding gigs.  They do take a little getting used to with page turns on the fly (plastic sheeting 3-ring binder books), but this is easily the best solution to wind issues.  Great product, works on all types of music stands...

product_title: Hohner 4 Piece Baby Band
review_body: Bought these a few weeks ago for my baby's 1st birthday and love them. She is the perfect age for them and my 2 older kids play along with her. Definetly recommend them and for a good price too!

product_title: Colorful Soprano Ukulele
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body: I plan on teaching myself how to pay and I refused to pay more than $40 on something I wasn't even sure I'd like. I love this ukulele. The color is pretty close to the picture. I took every ones advice and bought new strings but they haven't been delivered yet. I know nothing about ukulele's but I can tell that better strings will make a difference. Other than strings I don't have any problems with the ukulele. The bag is cheap but it also came free with the instrument. It's good for keeping the dust off it while you aren't playing. Great choice if you're a beginner and you don't want to overpay.

product_title: Pyle-Pro PPMCL15 - 15ft. Symmetric Microphone Cable XLR Female to XLR Male
review_body:
I got 5 of these to use to mic a drum kit in my small home studio. They'll be connected to a snake that runs from my PreSonus FireStudio Project. They should be okay for that purpose since they won't be connected / disconnected or moved or used in live applications. My concern is that one of the cables had a screw missing, leaving the male connector floating in the housing. A screw in the same location on another cable was loose. I think the screws could come loose if the cables were being connected / disconnected often such as if they were being used in a gigging situation. I haven't actually used them yet so can't comment on that aspect, but I'm sure that I couldn't tell the difference between these or any other cable by listening to them.
I gave them 4 stars for now - they are okay for what you'd expect at this price range and for my stationary application. If there wasn't the problem with the screws I'd give them a 5.
I ordered these on 6/30/2012 and received them on 7/5/2012 (there was a holiday during that time).

product_title: Buffet Crampon E-11 France Intermediate Bb Clarinet
review_body: After playing expensive Selmer clarinets, I tried the Buffet E11. I had my repairman check it over; he was amazed at the wood, and overall quality of the instrument. He said it's better than some of the R13's he's seen. The most important part of the clarinet is the mouth piece. I use a Clark Forbes (San Francisco) CWF mouthpiece with a 3 1/2 reed. It gives me a big, open tone. The horn is very responsive, an excellent value. I play classical. I love it!

product_title: Jack Deville Click-Less True-Bypass System and Switch

product_title: Stagg SG-50BK Tripod Guitar Stand with Folding Legs - Black
review_body: This is really a nice guitar stand.  It is so light weight and yet holds the heavy electric guitar.  This also folds for easy transport.  Good buy!

product_title: Sonic Barrier 1" Acoustic Foam w/PSA 18" x 24"
review_body:
I ordered two of these to put around one of my computers. It definitely helps with the noise.

I like these enough to want to get more, but I'll wait and see if the price drops. When (and if) it does, I'll probably pick of 5 more or so to put in some key spots near some noise makers (mostly other computers).

So 4 stars overall. I'm dropping a star for price since it can get fairly expensive when you buy several of these and also have to pay shipping on top of it, and these seem like they are made of inexpensive (yet effective) foam. If price weren't an issue, then I'd give it 5 stars.

product_title: Music Hall Cruise Control 2.0 Selectable 33/45 RPM Outboard Control for Music Hall Turntables
review_headline: I actually use this on a Music Hall turntable!
review_body: Unlike the other reviewers of this product, I use the Cruise Control 2.0 on a Music Hall turntable (MMH 5.1SE).  In conjunction with a KAB speed strobe, I can lock in the turntable speed to within 99.99% accuracy.  The Cruise Control is rock solid in holding the speed of the turntable at the set rate without any variation whatsoever (as measured by the KAB strobe).  The reason for using this or a similar product is that turntable speed, if it is inaccurate, can detrimentally effect the pitch of the playback and actually cause things to sound out of tune.  In theory, inaccurate speed can also reduce the dynamic range of a recording, but I'm not sure if that's marketing hype or not.  Anyway, the unit works great and actually looks and feels well built.

product_title: Pyle-Pro PMX1208 - 12 Channel 1000 Watts Powered Mixer
review_body: This is a 12 channel mixer with a lot of power. I use mine for live show and everything plugs in and powers up nicely. product_title: Dunlop  Nylon Standard Guitar Picks

product_title: Sennheiser HD 202 II Professional Headphones (Black)
review_body: This is my second pair of this headphone, one for home and one to leave at work. High quality sound and very long cord is great. My first pair has lasted a year and has not broken.

product_title: Logisys Blue 5 LED Lazer Light
review_body: Hooked this up to my 12\\" infinity subwoofer, and now whenever the bass hits, or there's a loud/scary part in a movie, it's like lightning sets off. I'm about to purchase another one.

product_title: Hohner Kids / Glockenspiel (Xylophone) with Songbook
review_body: Excellent sound, no matter who is playing with it, it doesn't annoy you. It's slim lined and compact. Mallet holders are great so it can be stored all as once piece.

product_title: Danelectro CD1 Cool Cat Distortion Pedal
review_body: First and foremost, I am not a boutique only, high strung guitarist. I like tones that I like; I'm simple that way. This pedal, however, sounds absolutely terrible. I have a Bugera V22 amp which has an alright gain channel (I actually quite like it) and its gain channel blows this pedal out of the water. I had a DS-1 for a little while but I returned it because it was only ok, but this pedal is far worse than that. I have a Rat 2 right now, which I love, and for about $30 more it is such a better deal. So why is it bad? Well, I had my amp's volume on 4 (which is actually pretty loud) and right when I turned the Cool Cat on it turned the volume way too high! I thought my Rat 2 added a lot of volume, but it was nothing compared to this crazy-buzzing-sounds-like-speakers-are-going-to-explode sound. So I turned my amps volume way down and it sounded the same, just quieter. After fooling around with it after a while I realized that if I didn't use a pick the sound became bearable. I tried everything with this pedal, tried to like it because everyone was raving how it sounded like an OCD, but it just doesn't. But I will give it two stars for being somewhat usable if you don't use a pick and set it just right.

product_title: Fender Locking Tuners Chrome
review_headline: Good quality,  you may need tools and skills
review_body: Out of the package the tuners seem to be of a very good quality.  Nice and tight, finish was perfect.  Be aware 3 of these are shorter for the top three strings.  A few things you should be aware of:  This is a replacement for Fender guitars.  I do believe these to be very good quality tuners. The rest of the review I will explain my experience and perhaps help others make a choice.  I was replacing the junky tuners on a 91 peavey predator, and I had to do a lot of drilling.  You may need to have some patience and decent skills if you are putting these on another brand of guitar.  I found a link on the net for installation tips and it really helped.  In the end I had to return them because my headstock was apparently thicker than a Fender headstock, and the shorter tuner axles were so short (1/8\\") you couldn't put strings on.  So like I say, its a pretty good product, but be aware they may not work on your off brand guitar.

review_body:

product_title: Traveler Guitar EG-2 Electric Travel Guitar
review_body: This baby is perfect for travel. Length, weight and portability are perfect. The travel case is well designed and built tough. The sound produced,through your home amp system or using the built in amp,(you will need headphones for the built in amp),is outstanding. The action is low and is just plain fun to play. The distortion setting....\\"DST\\",is awesome,and puts an element of heavy R&R sounds at your fingertips. This is an excellent guitar to ease the pain and insecurity of learning for beginners and new guitarist. It features a full size neck but because of it's overall size and playability it is much easier to get a feel for playing scales and learning notes. Even smaller hands will be able to move about the neck on this jewel. Just make sure you have a supply of 9 volt batteries to carry in the travel case. It will go through them when left connected in the compartment in the back. I generally remove the battery when I'm done playing through the headphones but if you forget,...it will drain it down. I bought mine as a Daily Deal and it was money well spent. NOTE; I've discovered the three way switch will TURN OFF the battery usage when you flip to the OFF position. I would still keep a extra 9 volt handy for your travels.

product_title: Colorful Soprano Ukulele
review_body: The packaging was a big box but that's okay.  I recycle.  Just know, despite what other reviews possibly say, this is NOT a toy.  I'm a self-taught uke player & I've been playing on a toy uke for over a year now.  I learned because I was a Day Care Teacher & wanted something fun and different for the kids in circle time.  I originally purchased a plastic SpongeBob uke from Toy'R Us so I KNOW what a toy Uke is.  Despite it's smallness this Mahalo U-30BU is a real Uke.  Its a soprano Uke so of coarse its suppose to be small.  Some of the other reviewers seem surprised by its size.  As for the strings, mine were black though the picture shows them as white (I'm sure for visual purposes.)  Its light weight and easy to manage.  As mentioned in several reviews you do have to tune it often at first.  That is common for a new instrument.  You don't necessarily have to replace the strings.  You just have to \\"break it in\\" like you would a new pair of shoes or blue jeans.  Even if you replace the strings, you still gotta tune it so.....get a tuner if you want.  Sure you can change the strings if you want to too but don't feel that you have to.  My new Uke had a \\"knick\\" in the fret board that was pretty noticeable but didn't affect the ability to play.  Though the name on the uke is Mahalo, there is a \\"Made In China\\" sticker on the back.  That made me snicker.  On my first day of having it the \\"knick\\" no longer bothered me after playing it because now I see the knick as part of the uke's character (as we all have that one freckle, mole, ect. about ourselves.)  So don't worry about a drip of paint or something if it doesn't affect the sound.  The black paint from the fret board did rub off on my fingertips a little but I was okay with that.  I actually enjoy the pains and trials of learning a new Ukulele song.  I look forward to wearing the paint off. (Yeah, I'm weird, I'm writing a review on a ukulele okay?)  I originally bought a toy uke because I wasn't sure if I was going tostick with it.  But here I am nearly a year and a half later.  No longer a Day Care Teacher but still playing my ukulele.  Now I wished I had bought this Mahalo uke instead of the toy because I have some getting used to of a bit larger fret to deal with but I'm okay with that.  Compared to my SpongeBob plastic (which actually sounded pretty good) this Mahalo sounds great!  And its a couple of dollars less than the toy!  Its pretty and fun.  I love it.  My Uke is my \\"magic blue pill\\" that chases my blues away so the blue color was important to me.  Sure I plan on replacing the strings with blue ones soon but that isn't stopping me from having a blast with my new \\"Bluke\\" pill right now.  If you're thinking of starting the Uke and buying this one.....DO!  It's not that much money and so worth the investment.  There are tons of resources out there on the internet to learn to play and this Ukulele is perfect for a beginner or some one wanting one for easy mobility and fun!!! Buy this uke and then strum like you mean it!  I'm a blogger....[...]

product_title: D'Addario DIY Solderless Pedalboard  Kit, 10 feet, 10 plugs
review_body: After looking at the George L's and Lava's I bought two of these kits to connect the pedals on my PedalTrain board. My decision was based mostly on the price diference, which is substantial if you need to make more than five cables, but also on the fact that I've had good luck with other Planet Waves gear I own.  I found it hard to judge the quality of the kit from the online pictures but was very pleased with the look and feel of the plugs and cable. The plug housings are heavy and nicely finished in a mirror-like silver gray. The entire plug barrel is gold plated as is the grounding screw. The cable is pretty flexible for coax.  Making the cables couldn't be simpler. Cut the cable to the length you want with the included cutter (it mushrooms the end a little so you have to roll it between your fingers a bit to round it back out), twist on the plug housings and fully tighten the grounding screws. Takes less than a minute per cable. I checked the finished cables with an ohm meter to verify the connections and every one was good on the first try. I pulled and twisted the cable and connectors a fair amount and still had good contact. I feel confident that these will hold up well on my pedal board and they look and sound great.

review_body: I do not own this pedal board, but the guitarist in my band does.
