product_title: Lanikai SM-T Custom Series Spalted Mango Tenor Ukulele
review_body: This Uke really does sound as good as it looks, has such a warm tone to it. Its pretty much a 'perfect' Mango Wood Tenor. It arrived packaged very protected and on time.   If you have any doubts I'm telling you now you will not regret buying this beautiful ukulele 10/10!

product_title: Ebtech Hum X Voltage Hum Filter
review_body: I was skeptical about this product.  But it worked to remove an annoying whine in my computer speakers when my graphics card was under load.  I even bought an external sound card, Presonus Firebox, to help with the whine but it didn't stop it in the least.  In fact, I just heard the whine more clearly.    I have no idea how or why it works.  But it worked perfectly for me.

product_title: Humes & Berg Stonelined Symphonic Str. Red/White Alumnium Trombone Mute (126)
review_body: Gave it 5 stars. My silver trombone (King 3b) (which sounds like a kazoo, when muted) sounds like a muted trombone. Would buy another without hesitation, should the needed arrive.

product_title: Vic Firth 5A Nova Drum Sticks (Nylon Tip, 12 Pair)
review_body: Twelve pairs of this Nova drumsticks lasted to me the same of one pair of regular Vic Firth 5AN. They broke easily in ways you could never imagine like in 10 seconds of playing a simple rock groove they cracked cleanly about 1 inch from the tip with no reason. I think there is no quality control at all for these things (because definitly they aren't drumsticks). Believe me, never buy Nova sticks (unless you want them to set a fire). I am a guy who read profoundly every opinion people leave in the products I'm interested to in amazon and is really useful for my pre-buying selection process. When I bought this 12-pack there was no customer reviews so I decided to take my risks and buy, it appears to be such a bargain but it was not. product_title: Gibson Les Paul Junior Electric Guitar, Satin Cherry - Chrome Hardware
review_headline: Les Paul Junior Rules! Elegance in simplicity.
review_body: I'm a stratocaster player and after reading about the Les Paul Jr being an under-appreciated guitar, I decided to check them out. It has a nice fat sound you don't expect from a single coil pickup. The neck has nice feel, very comfortable, at least compared to the Gibson SG standard (had that for a year, never got comfortable with it) and the Les Paul Studio (just too darn unwieldy). It's a great value, great tone and a fine looking instrument. Just look how that neck just melds with the body, that's American craftsmanship at its best.  My only beef is that Gibson doesn't make a LP Jr hardcase, instead you get a gigbag, oh well, better than nothing.

product_title: Palatino VC-450 Allegro Cello Outfit with Carrying Bag, 4/4 Size
review_body: I am very pleased with my cello which was a surprise 2010 Christmas present from my husband.  It has a lovely tone and the price made it affordable for a first cello. My son, who is a music teacher was happy with how it sounded and was helpful with inital setup.  Because, like all string instruments, it needed some adjustment time, I had 3 strings break in quick succession(within the first ten days). This was scary but has resolved.  During this time, I found a violin shop which helped with my last string and advice.  Just this week, this shop made a new bridge for this instrument and replaced the tailpiece with a German-made tailpiece with better fine-tuners.  I am more pleased as this made it easier to play and tune.  The original fine tuners did not work well(so I just tuned with the pegs - no real problem).  All this to say that the sound is very nice and the price allowed me to begin learning the cello.  I love to play and average playing/practicing one to two hours daily on this instrument.

I bought my ukulele at a guitar store and didn't get a case with it because they were too expensive...but after having it 8 months, I decided I needed to get a bag because I'd be taking it on a plane. product_title: Auralex GRAMMA 2.75 Inches High
review_body: I've had this for a few months now.  I'm using it to support a Hsu VTF-2 MK3 subwoofer.  Anybody who has this sub knows it`s a sub with a very large cabinet.  Originally, I had the sub half on tile floor and half on carpeting.  I`d cut a couple of pieces of carpet to put underneath as per the manufacturer`s instructions, but every time I looked at that setup, I was less than satisfied.    Well, the GRAMMA solved my problem.  My sub completely covers the logo etc., and looks if it`s just sitting on the floor.  Other reviewers have commented on the superior performance of their subs using this unit, and while I can`t necessarily make that claim, I can tell you it does what it`s supposed to do!     The product is well made - very neat and clean.  It probably doesn`t cost the manufacturer very much to produce, but there aren`t a lot of options out there.  I also bought the Subdude (reviewed separately).  Money well spent.

product_title: Behringer Ultravoice Xm8500 Dynamic Vocal Microphone, Cardioid
review_body: I purchased this studio microphone because I was previously searching for the perfect headset for screencasting.  I have always been particularly picky in headsets and headphones and work best with ones that are a full ear-cup binaural type.  After months of searching, testing, trying and failing I realized that I already had the perfect headphones that I love to death, a pair of Sennheisers.  Funny thing is they are older and the available headsets from Sennheiser do not replicate this comfort level for me.  So this finally brings me to this microphone.  I wanted something better than the Logitech USB mic that is available but also did not want to spend the money for a Yeti if I did not have to.  This Behringer studio mic works awesome coupled with an inexpensive desk stand and male XLR to 3.5mm cable/adapter.  My headphones are not wireless, but have a 20 foot cable on them.  I can easily walk across the room and Captivate and the Behringer will adjust to pick up my voice flawlessly.  I have less background noise in my screencasts as well making them far more professional without the expense.  I have had no issues with popping or breathing noises on Captivate so the windscreen seems to be more than adequate.  In the end I feel like this microphone at this price point has so many uses and really allows those of us not working in studios per se to access the next level of quality without spending a fortune to do so.  NOTE:  If you see this mic for a decent price on Amazon, don't think about it , just order it.  This item seems to fluctuate daily by $3 to even $10.

product_title: Planet Waves Auto-Trim Tuning Machines, 6 In-Line setup, Gold
review_body: These have worked as advertised for me.  I've had them on two electric guitars - a 6-string for a few years, and recently equipped a 12-string with them.  The locking feature makes string changes occur in minutes.  The auto trim feature snips excess string cleanly and effortlessly.  The 18:1 ratio makes accurate tuning quite easy.  They're very solid-feeling.  The guitars that they are installed on stay in tune longer than my other guitars.    The plated portion of the finish appears deep, and looks like it will last a while.  The flat black peg won't go with every guitar finish.

product_title: Wittner MT50 Quartz Metronome
review_headline: You pay for what you get.
review_body: This device is the best for its price.  As for the cons mentioned in other reviews, I would use a 1/8 jack thin output cord through a mini PA device if it isn't loud enough. (Its the same cord width used for IPod earbuds)  Any old stereo tuner would do if you have a female socket 'in' as well as your speaker line 'out'. You may have to buy a cheap converter of 1/8 to L + R audio input jack but someones always got that laying around their house/apartment if they got a stereo receiver.  Caution: that metal stand on the back can become unattached and bang around on the insides of the PC board if you dropped it like me.  (Don't drop it too often.)  However, the casing is made of a much more solid plastic than others for the price.

product_title: Emerson GQ756 CDG Karaoke Player
review_body: Has a lot of nice features - I'm running through an amp for better sound and through a TV for easier to see graphics.  Well worth the cost.

product_title: Semi Hollow Electric Guitar with Flamed Maple Top
review_headline: Not bad but not a $500 dollar guitar
review_body: Well it looks like I am the first to review this guitar. First off dont let the pics fool you this thing is tiny, its not a wide body jazz guitar although it may look like one in some of the pics. Its smaller than a fender, almost like a kid sized guitar. I like it because it has a wood body and its a nice looking guitar. I noticed even with no amp it has a quiet acoustic sound probably due to its wooden body. The action was way off and the top E string had a terrible buzzing noise when you strummed it. It took some adjusting of the bridge panel to take the buzzing away. The action had to be set pretty high in order to remedy this. It came with a truss rod tool but I dont have the experience to mess with something like that. It does sound good now after adjusting however. Some of the craftsmenship is shoddy I must admit, on the neck made in china there are several inconsistancies in the frets, for instance on some of the frets edges are sanded too far so you can see the edge of the fret through the wood finnish where other spots look like they should. I mean its smooth but the neck looks poorly made. Also the plastc string board at the top of the neck that holds the strings in place is not at all flush with the wood like it should be on one side and the plastic looks really cheap. Some of the tuning heads are really loose to the point where if you turn it a whole turn it barely changes 1/2 an octave so its hard to get it perfectly in tune and some of the strings come out of tune easily while others stay perfectly in tune while playing. Some of the wood on the body has deep ridges or pits or dips for lack of a better word. In the pics you can see in the F holes the wood backing exposed has a smooth natural wood color where the wood isnt finnished, on the one I got the wood on the inside was very coarse, unsanded and painted black with spray paint or soemthing. Through the F Holes you can see a lot of wires with cheap masking style tape wrapped around them. In the chrome base where you feed in the strings there is some kind of paper material sticking out between the bolt that holds the base to the wood most likely to act as a wedge. I'm not sure if they drilled or sanded the hole oversized but the paper sticking out is rather unsightly and will probably be a pain to remove with a razor tool. Something they should have done while manufacturing in my opinion. Another area has a spot where the flamed finnish wasnt applied properly and has a lima bean sized whiteish spot on the otherwise beautiful finnish, and instead of fixing the blemish they just went ahead and clear coated over the permanent blemish. There are many other blemishes throughout the guitar finnish, tiny speckles, painting anomalies where the paint had bled or dripped making a paint bump or bubble they just clear coated over and didnt sand down or fix. Perhaps I'm being too harsh but I want to be thorough since there are no ther reviews and these things are important to mention. On the bright side it plays well after some adjustments, looks nice if you dont look too closely and its relatively cheap at $200 bucks. I kinda wish I had spent $100-200 more and got a epiphone jazz style guitar which is what I wanted. What I got was a miniature knock off version of that. The customer service of Davison was great i must say. But overall the guitar wasnt quite what I wanted but I'm not one to return things. I guess the moral of the story is when you by something online, especially something you have never seen in person, your probably not gonna get quite what you want. If you want a cheaply priced, nice looking, decent sounding guitar then by all means give this one a shot. It does have a nice wooden body sound. Oh also it came with a double guitar stand and a chord which was nice, especially since it didnt indicate that in the description.

product_title: American Dj 24" Black Light Fixture w/ LAMP Black-24BLB
review_body: I ordered two of these.  Both turned on for a split second and that was it.  Very cheaply made.  Do not waste you time, you get what you pay for.

product_title: Clarke SBDC Pennywhistle Boxed, Key of D
review_headline: Hard to play, but great whistle.
review_body: [[VIDEOID:mo17D8A8UHRBACZ]]The whistle was shipped the very next day after I ordered it, and it arrived two days later. Very pleased. As for the whistle itself, it is VERY difficult to play compared to my Oak Classic key of C whistle. When you get it and first start playing it, chances are you'll start out playing the second octave. It takes an insane amount of air control to play the first octave, because it requires little to no breath, and it is VERY soft and quiet. This new whistle does sound amazing though. It's crystal clear. 4/5 for the product because of how quiet the lowest octave is. 5/5 for the seller.  EDIT: After playing around with the whistle for a couple hours, I'd like to change my rating to 5/5. It took a lot of effort, but I've figured out how to play the lowest register better. Now I can play it at that volume where it sounds soft enough to make that beautiful, mellow sound, but loud enough to for people to hear and enjoy. When you first get this whistle, don't give up on it. Make sure you use a VERY small amount of air to play it, otherwise you WILL start out playing in the second register and you'll be upset when you find it near impossible to reach the third register. (That's right. I'm implying that, in the right hands, this whistle could potentially play three octaves.) Great buy!  In the video, I play the beginning of the song \\"Concerning Hobbits\\" from the Lord of the Rings trilogy on the Clarke Original Penny Whistle \\"D\\" that I bought here. (I have about 6 hours playing experience total on the tin whistle, which is why I lack the ability to play ornamentation.)  Enjoy.

review_body: I've been using these for a month and so far I do not have any major complaints. The only thing is that when I wear these headphones and my so-called \\"hipster\\" glasses, they sort of bother me. Other than that, these headphones are fantastic!

product_title: Korg BA40 Bluegrass Tuner for Mandolin, Fiddle, Banjo and Resonator Guitar
review_body: large lcd display, compact, 3-yr warranty, and competitively-priced.  it's a solid chromatic tuner which is accurate enough to use for saddle tuning adjustments on my Floyd Rose tremolo.  a good product from a reputable company and worth the money.

product_title: Blue Yeti USB Microphone - Blackout Edition
review_body: As expected, after reading all the other reviews on the microphone, when I tested it on my own computer, sound was high quality and did not disappoint me. Thing is built like a tank. If you have trouble with sound, try adjusting the setting behind the microphone. Thanks for such an awesome microphone.

product_title: On Stage FS7850B Guitar Foot Rest
review_body: This is a fairly straight-forward product; it's a guitar foot rest. It works as advertised and is durable. The rubber feet hold very well, especially on a wood floor. I purposely tried sliding it and it takes quite a bit of effort. It also holds well on carpet due to the friction from the rubber.   It's adjustable from very low to very high, I prefer somewhere in the middle. I play steel string fingerstyle, and I play a few classical pieces. I don't play in the classical position often, but I do from time to time. I also use the footrest when playing on my right leg (right-handed player) and it is comfortable as well.   Great price, too.

product_title: Aottop Hand Strengtheners
review_headline: Not just good for your fret hand.
review_body: I play bass and recently decided to wing myself off a pick.  I had the dexterity but not the endurance to play hours with out a pick. I bought this to strengthen both my hands while I am on the phone at work.  So far it has worked wonders.  I have used it just a few min at a time 6-12 times a day and I no longer have a problem with my right wrist feeling fatigued.      The only complaint I have (which does not affect me so much) is this is probably too stiff for a new players pinky's finger.    Please excuse any spelling mistakes.

product_title: CBI Instrument Cable
review_body: These cables are made from top quality components and expertly assembled in the USA.  I had one just like this with the Neutrik connectors (gave away as gift) and now have two with the G&H Show Saver connector option.  This makes them similar to some boutique cables that cost three times the price.    These cables are well-balanced with articulate mids and highs and tight bass.  They are well-shielded, look nice, and handle well.    You could pay more for gold plating for slightly better corrosion resistance or for woven coverings to make the wire look cute, if you want to.

product_title: Green Acoustic Guitar with Green Harmonica
review_body: This was above and beyond what we were expecting!!!  It is a gorgeous color and has an amazing sound!!!  We were so very impressed!  The seller was great with answering our questions as well.  We would highly recommend this product!!!  We were overly pleased!!!

product_title: Peavey AmpKit Link Electric Guitar Interface for iPhone, iPad, and iPod Touch
review_headline: had problems, but solved by Peavey
review_body: I recently purchased the Ampkit LINK.  I chose it based on various reviews which suggested that, as an active device (batteries are included) it handles feedback and bass better than its competitors (I play bass).  When it arrived, it did not work properly (you can read other user reviews here and elsewhere for a description of the problems, they were exactly the same).  After some websearching, I found information on the Peavey forums about how to handle the problem.  If you contact info (at) agilepartners (dot) com they will be able to ship you a replacement that does not have the problem.  If you simply return it to Amazon, I don't believe they have any way to tell whether the replacement is defective as well.    My replacement Ampkit LINK from Peavey works fine, and was shipped at their expense.  It took a bit longer than I had hoped, but it's here.  So, now I can actually review it.    It works, and does what it's supposed to just fine.  I haven't had any feedback problems, or issues with the bass not coming through.  The one complaint I have, now that it's working, is it feels like a cheaply constructed plastic toy.  Because it's so light it also has a tendency to be dragged around by the instrument cable if you aren't sitting very still, which seems to me it could eventually lead to issues with the connection to the iOS device.  But other than that, no complaints at all.

product_title: Laptop Stand - Black
review_body: First off the screws would not fit in the areas they were supposed to go in. Secondly, box was not packaged, merely taped up on the sides and sent to me like that. Overall, I would never recommend this product to anyone or the person who sold it.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH Professional Studio Monitor Headphones
review_body: I purchased these originally as a value-conscious solution for neutral/accurate headphones for mixing and studio work.  Having previously owned Monster Turbines, Bose QC3, Bose Triports, Sony XB-700s, Koss PortaPros and the like.  I found that they were a whole new realm of musical representation for me.  The bass is rich but never ever overpowering.  The mids are more prominent than in any other headphone I'd heard, and the highs are very well represented while simultaneously being non-fatiguing.  Noise-cancellation is effective; I've used this for live mixing while drums are playing right behind me.  The soundstage is a smidgen small because it is a closed-back headphone of course, but at this price with this technology, the total package is well worth it.  Let's just say that while you may be curious how other headphones sound, you definitely won't be disappointed by how these sound, especially relative to the price range.

product_title: Casio CTK-2100 61 Key Personal Keyboard with New Voice Pad Feature
review_body: Picked this up to see if I wanted to learn to play piano. Glad I did, great cheap way to start a fun hobby.

product_title: Korg KAOSSCASE Nylon Travel Case for KAOSSILATOR or miniKP
review_body: This item came on time, in good conditions, it is doing exactly what it is supposed to!

product_title: CHAUVET DJ Hurricane 1100 Fog Machine | Fog Machines
review_headline: Make sure you turn off your fire alarm!
review_body:
This machine is much smaller than anticipated. Roughly the size of a large shoe box. Set up is brainless. It heats up in less than 5 minutes, and for such a tiny device, it puts out plenty of fog. Filled up my whole house and set off the fire alarms in about two minutes.

I also like the fact that it's pretty quiet. I've seen youtube reviews that made me worry that this would be very noisy, but it's not. Their is an intermittent pump noise and nozzle noise, but really not bad at all.

Highly recommended.

product_title: Yamaha P95 Digital Piano Bundle with Bench, Stand, Triple Pedal Board, Headphones, Book, and Dust Cover - Black
review_body: I got this keyboard set a few weeks ago. Generally it's great. Nice tone, and so on. Only the stool is a bit basic. product_title: PYLE-PRO PPHP1599AI - 15'' 1600 Watt Portable Powered 2 Way Full Range Loud Speaker System w/Built in MP3/USB & Ipod Dock
review_headline: Great for the price... iPod dock poorly implemented.
review_body: I bought this speaker for personal use. The speaker was delivered within two days of purchase (I chose standard shipping). The sound is great! For the price, I think it's a great speaker. There's only one problem; The built-in iPod dock is a great idea very poorly implemented. If you play the speakers loud enough the vibration will make your iPod disconnect/undock and your favorite song will stop playing immediately... and we don't want that, do we? If you use an iPhone the vibration will skip the song and eventually the iPhone will be disconnected as well. Oh, and iPhones charging is not supported by the built-in iPod dock.    Pros:    Other than standard features of a powered speaker, good sound quality, built-in interface to  navigate external hard drives, light weight, 1600Watts/low price, many inputs, Ships quickly.    Cons:    iPod dock poorly implemented. iPod pops out because of the vibration.    I haven't tortured the speaker for a couple of hours yet. I'll post an update after I throw a party and see how it handles it.    UPDATE: I was not able to torture the speaker. When I plugged it in for the party it never produced a sound! :-s Luckily I had a backup. This item only worked the first time for me and never worked again :-(

product_title: Line 6 POD Studio UX2 USB w/2 Free 20' Mic cables and 2 Free 18.6' Instrument cables
review_body: This unit is an amazing piece of equipment.  It is extremely versatile in its application; there are tons of amp models available to suit any type of music.  The presets are it's only weak point, especially in the high-gain area.  However, once you learn how to use the included software (POD Farm) to it's fullest capability, you can get tones that are nearly indistinguishable from those of high-end tube amplifiers (on recordings, at least).    I also use this as an audio interface for my Korg M50 workstation.  The recording quality is crystal clear and the latency is negligible.  This is an excellent unit for someone who is an amateur producer like myself. product_title: Hohner Super Chromonica Chromatic Harmonica, Key of A
review_headline: This is the BEST Harmonica I've EVER played!
review_body: Folks, I've been playing harmonica seriously since 1985, when I started on a Hohner Marine Band C diatonic, and have played publicly since 1999, when I played for a while with blues/folk singer Ruthie Foster. Last year, I upgraded to a Hohner Educator 10 hole Chromatic and then to a 12 hole Chrometta Chromatic. They were okay, but the bars would occasionally get stuck and I would have to pump them repeatedly before playing.    I always liked the harps in the key of A, because of their richer, deeper tone, so now that I am good at playing Chromatics in public, I decided to go for this. I read that Stevie Wonder and Larry Adler played Hohner Super Chrominica Chromatics, and I learned from playing Cds of their music, so I thought I'd give it a try. I had also read and heard that these are to Chromatic harmonicas what the Stradavarious is to violins and Steinway is to pianos.    Ladies and gentlemen, the Hohner Super Chromonica Chromatic is hands down the BEST Harmonica I've EVER played!    The bar is very short, so there is no sticking when changing keys nor is there a need to \\"pump\\" the instrument before playing. Plus, it has a beautiful, deep, and full-throated tone, which is great especially if you like wah-wah and tremlo effects while playing. All of this led to some easy and soulful playing. I spent three hours straight playing and rehearsing on this thing after getting it in the mail. I could not stop with my Chromatic addiction. Made me want to grab this harmonica and play with it all night long (to paraphrase Ray Parker). I almost NEVER want to even touch a diatonic after the joy of playing this harmonica.    The only slight complaint about this is that the case is too bulky. I like to travel with a harmonica in my pocket to play whenever I'm ready.     Trust me fellow harmonicists, you will truly become a Chromatic addict after playing this. This makes me want to place a dozen roses on Matthias Hohner's grave.

product_title: Johnson FX-300 Analog Delay Pedal
review_headline: Know what you're getting and you'll do fine
review_body: I just received my pedal and gave it a run through.  Not bad at all for the money.  That being said, here's the good and bad:    The bad - The pedal arrived DOA.  It lit up, and dry signal came through ok, but no effect.  I saw another review at Harmony Central where someone pointed out a micro pot inside the unit that allowed you to change the range of delay times, so I thought maybe that pot had corrosion from sitting a long time.  Sure enough, I took the pedal apart, turned the pot a few times, and it works fine now.  I also dialed in some longer delay times.  Out of the box it only does around 300ms max.  Now mine does around 450ms.   If I turned that little pot all the way, it would probably do around 800 or so.       The So So - The overall sound quality is decent, but far from pristine.  I plan to use mine with fairly heavy distortion 90% of the time, and used that way there is hardly any noticeable difference in tone with the unit switched on or off.  When I played through it clean and without any other effects in the chain it did take a little out of the sound.  If you play alot of clean or slightly broken up tones, you may get annoyed.   If you're not a purist, then you'll probably be happy.  If you make your living playing, just buy better gear!    The good - It was like $40 and it works!  The controls are simple and effective, and it sounds decent.  I don't know why they don't give the full range of delay time with the control knob, but oh well...  get your geek on and open it up!    One more piece of advice, know what your looking for.  There is a big difference between an \\"Echo\\" pedal and a \\"Delay\\" pedal.  This is completely meant to be an Echo pedal.  This means that the echos occurring are not meant to sound exactly like the input signal.  They are \\"dirtied up\\" a bit to mimic an old tape delay.  The amount of \\"dirty\\" is controlled by the Quality knob, but even on the cleanest setting it still has a slight effect on the tone of the echo.  This isn't because of a fault in the pedal, that's what an echo does.  If you want digitally replicated repeats, you won't be happy.  You should get a Digital Delay pedal.    I gave it 4 stars because it arrived dead and had to be revived, and the dry side of the signal could be a little cleaner.  It'll be plenty of fun to mess with for the low price I paid.

product_title: Keeley Electronics Java Boost Guitar Effect Pedal
review_headline: Old school booster disguised as a new box.
review_body: I just got this several days ago and tried it with my telecaster into a 71' blackfaced Pro Reverb. The pedal has a tone knob that cuts highs, and a level knob for output volume. There is a three position switch that is mid boost, high boost, and full range boost. Set for high boost it is the Dallas Rangemaster treble boost circuit. In the high or mid boost it cuts a little bit of bass from your tone but kicks up your highs or mids(depending on the switch)probably 5db or so. Full range probably the same but everything is boosted so no bass loss. What is cool to me is everything runs thru a NOS transistor that adds a grainy, very light distortion to your tone. This you can't adjust. You set your amp into just breaking up and step on this to get a kick in the frequency you selected, and use the level knob to load up your input gain. Running the output knob at 12:00 is a little boost and if you turn it way up your probably sending 25 or so db into your amp. It's not a distortion box on its own, just a kick in the pants of your guitar signal. I used to do the same basic idea with a Boss 7 band EQ. Kick up low/mids and add several db's of output level. With the Boss and TS 808 overdrive pedals out there, your buying somebody elses idea of what a good sound is, and some of those sound great. I have several of those pedals, but then so do a million other guitar players. This Java Boost does an adjustable volume boost, but adds the grainy, barely there sixties distortion. It fattened my tele rear pickup into a thick, but not dark sounding guitar. The circuit is from the mid sixties and rumor is Eric Clapton used one when he recorded the Bluesbreakers album. A vintage Rangemaster is well over $1000.00 if you could find one in working order. This is the same circuit, with some other boost options that don't alter the original treble boost design if it's in the treble boost option on the three way switch. I prefer the mid boost myself, but that was with the tele and the Pro Reverb. With my Les Paul and my JCM 800 I may run it totally different. My only other boost pedal on my board is a Nano LPB 1 by EH. They are only $40.00 so I'm not just buying expensive stuff to impress my friends. They are a great pedal also for kicking your amp. The Java just has its uses. Very pleased with it.

product_title: Quantum Leap Symphonic Orchestra Silver Edition Virtual Instrument
review_body: You will be able to find demos showcasing the instruments in this library, and they will sound very good, and they really do. But this review is about telling prospective buyers what they DON'T tell you.  MOST of the instruments in this library have NOTE RANGE LIMITATIONS! For example, their solo violin sounds awesome, but it has about a 3-octave limitation. How does that translate negatively? I had a cadenza in my music that somehow fell short about three notes in the lower range! When you exceed their note-range limitations, you hear silence! I ended up having to create a separate track and selecting a similar sounding instrument (in this case a viola) to compensate for the three notes that the solo violin could not provide!  I do understand why they did it this way though, and it's to preserve the fidelity of the sampled instruments. But it is in my humble opinion that they should've provided the full range anyway, even if they had to synthesize the remaining notes, and leave it to the judgement of the musician whether or not they would use those synthesized compensations.  These note-range limitations could turn your arrangement from being simple and organized to becoming a convoluted and messy fragmented arrangement. Musicians should not be restricted in this way.  Also, I found their installation documentation highly convoluted. If you think your installation will be a simple and smooth \\"Insert the DVD and sit back and wait\\", think again. When you receive the package, it comes with a sheet of instructions telling you that the DVDs are OUTDATED, and that you should download the latest version from their web site. What they didn't say was that you still had to use the outdated DVDs anyway or the instrument libraries won't get installed. But this will be just the beginning of your ordeal. In the interest of time and space in this review, I'm not going to enumerate all the steps you have to go through, but just be prepared for an unorthodox, convoluted process ofinstallation.  I was tempted to give this product a one-star, but the quality of their sampled instruments were excellent. I also liked how they provided different articulations for some of the key instruments like strings. For example, Violins would have a long/legato version, a staccato version, a tremolo version, an accented version, etc. Most instruments do not come with this level of refinement, but they are very good (as long as you do not exceed the note-range limitations!)  Buy this orchestral library if you want, but you have been forewarned!

product_title: Chauvet Dj COLORstrip Mini RGB 4-Channel LED Dam Linear Wash Light w/Automated & Sound-Active Programs
review_body:
I'm a solo musician that gigs in dark corners of dark bars. I needed something to add light and color to my stage areas without adding another trip to the car for lighting gear. I'm extremely happy with the Colorstrip Mini so far.

First off, the portability is great. Its about 19\\" long and light as a feather, seems very well constructed too. I just toss it in my gear box with cables, etc. Also, at $100 its an easy investment decision considering what it provides.

I just set it on the floor out in front of me, pointed at my chest (the adjustable mounting brackets double well as a floor stand). In my opinion, it is SUPER bright. Its amazing how such a physically small light source will wash the average size performance area especially if the room is dark. I personally don't find it to be too obtrusive having been in front of stage lights before but could see someone with sensitive eyes feeling differently. I can still easily see what's going on with my pedals on the floor and my mixing board. However, if you stare at it dead on, you will see \\"sun spots\\" when you look away. A little common sense helps avoid this issue.

I currently use the Colorstrip only as a standalone unit in its \\"Sound Active\\" modes. Other options include Master / Slave functionality (daisy chain up to 30+ units) and DMX control. Chauvet even makes a foot controller for it. I've been pretty happy with the internal programming for my purposes. You can do anything from a very subtle color-fading effect (022) to extremely dynamic, beat-following programs (008, 009) . The built-in mic cues the program changes very responsively. As soon as a beat kicks in, its following right along (1...2...3...4..., Red...Green...Blue...Yellow, etc.) Some of the programs follow the beat but with more gradual color changes (013, 015) or a clubby \\"lens- flipping\\" effect (012). There is even a \\"shuffle\\" program (023) that randomly runs through all the other programs. My only gripe with the programming is that the sound active functions kind of keep on running randomly even when the music stops. I would like to see it just stay on the color it was on when the song ended until it picks up significant sound again.

Overall, I'm having a lot of fun with it and might add one or two more down the road.

review_body: I received my Oscar Schmidt baritone uke and was very impressed by the fit and finish of the instrument.  It has a good feel to it, looks great and plays great.  It is better quality than what I had expected.  I have many fine guitars and this is a quality instrument.

product_title: American DJ Micro Galaxian Laser Special Effects Lighting
review_body: Brought this to a party. Had my mobile ipod sterio with me. Lasers went to the music and everyone at the party loved it. Highly recommend for some house parties. Going to use it again for my Halloween party this weekend. Going to wear my V for Vendetta costume and rock out.

product_title: Jade Violin Viola Cello Rosin
review_body: I was using a Pirastro Goldflex because I am in an very humid area, but when I used this one for the first time, my violin sounded so much better, everyone who listen when I play say that now I play beautiful, that sounds excellent! and It doesn't live more dust over the violin than the pirastro.

product_title: Latin Percussion LP305 Merengue Guiro
review_body: Our percussionist had been using a metal guiro/shaker combo but he wanted a larger guiro with a handle.  This one produces a bigger raspier sound and is good for large groups like ours.  It also looks substantial.

product_title: Fender By MeguiarS Guitar Care Ultimate Wipe Detailing Cloth
review_body: This cloth can get all the smudges and fingerprints off out your guitar without fear scratching or anything like that. However, it's not super easy like they advertise it to be and it tends to smear fingerprints around quite a bit before they come off. For 10 bucks on amazon it's a pretty good buy, but at the regular price of 15 would not be worth it.

product_title: Valencia VG-180CE Acoustic Electric Classical Guitar, High Gloss Amber Finish
review_body: I bought this Guitar a few months ago (27 april) I like it it's good Guitar very affordable and I like this Brand (Valencia) they have Great Guitars for good prices, I also uploaded several pictures here you can check them out, it also comes with built-in tuner it's electric as well so you can plug it into the amplifier I was going to get the Vg-190ce but it wasn't in stock at the time they look similar however, If you are going to buy this Guitar just go ahead and don't waste your time you will not be sorry, I would recommend it.

product_title: BEHRINGER XENYX 1002FX
review_headline: Look close before you buy this!
review_body: I bought this unit wanting just a few more features, as I currently have the XENYX802. I used the latter in a very compact portable stage setup, and I appreciated that in almost the exact same space, I now had a few additional input channels, along with build in effects. I have an external reverb in my 802 setup, so I figured this unit would save me some space. But look closely! This unit has no EQ adjust ability on anything other than its two mic channels. There are a few other compromises, and it all comes down to this... you can't add more channels, plus effects in the same space, without running out of room for controls, so some things had to go in this design. Ultimately i returned mine, as it also had a factory defect. But had that not been the case, I don't think I'd have been satisfied for long with the missing features, so in the end I took a refund rather than a replacement.

product_title: Shure SRH440 Professional Studio Headphones (Black)
review_body: I read all about these headphones and watched video reviews on the internet and tried to learn everything I could about the sound quality, value, comfort, and durability before I bought these. When I got them I was so excited to wear them, but as soon as I put them on, I hated them. Even with the excellent sound quality, you can't listen to them if you can't wear them comfortably. I strongly recommend going to a store where you can try them on before you wear them, because I could not stand the fact that the tips of my ears touched the inside cloth (which was supposed to protect your ears from sliding along the plastic interior and instead did nothing). I definitely have slightly bigger ears than the average person, but nothing even approaching ridiculously large. I sent these back immediately, and have learnt my lesson on trying something on before I order it.

product_title: Herco HE112P Flat Thumbpicks, Medium, 3/Player's Pack
review_body: I ordered these on a uTube recommendation and that proved to be a mistake.  The picks are made from a thinner than usual plastic and the thumb area does NOT hold the pick in place (on your thumb). On top of that, the 3 picks, in the package, are nested inside each other so when you pull them apart only the inner-most pick is even a \\"medium\\" size.  The other 2 are stretched out from being slipped over each other and are useless!  I would NOT recommend these to anyone.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH Professional Studio Monitor Headphones
review_body: I did tons of research before buying these, and was very impressed with the sound quality. They sounded awesome. I had to return them though, as they were horrendously uncomfortable. They are super clampy on the ears, but worst of all, the headband digs into your scalp something fierce. I was only able to stand them for about an hour, and two hours after that, the top of my head *still* hurt. Got the Beyerdynamic 770s, which feel like pillows in comparison.

product_title: Danelectro N10B Honey Tone Mini Amp in Burgundy
review_headline: You can't go wrong with this.
review_body: I was looking for a tiny amp I could shove under the table and out of the way when not in use.  This amp is about the size of two cans of cola sitting side by side.  It has plenty of volume for goofing around your living room.  It even has overdrive and a list of settings to achieve various sounds.  You can also plug headphones in, too (the same size jack that MP3 players have). Heck, I got the separate AC adapter but it will run off a battery, too.  So, grab the adapter and a cable and you can get free shipping from Amazon.

product_title: American Dj Quad Gem Dmx Led Powered Effect Light
review_body: I have two of these which I use at least 5 times a week in my mobile karaoke and DJ shows.  One is suspended from one of my light bars and the other I ste on the floor and aim it at the wall behind the show.  I set them both to run independently and I also use a haze generator which really makes these lights pop.  I play big venues and stages and this light covers a very large area with nice bright lights. I've been using one of these continuosly for over 2 years and the other about a year and a half.  Both have been trouble free.  Spend the money and get this light.

product_title: Hohner Harmonica HH1896-C Marine Band Harmonica - Key of C
review_headline: richer sound, easier to play than the Golden Melody
review_body:
I got this to replace my [[ASIN:B002B55RRS Hohner Golden Melody Harmonica, Key of C]] harp. Right out of the box it sounds richer, even though I've adjusted the reeds on my G. M. I was really surprised at how much better this harp sounds.

I also found it easier to hold and while I was worried the edges might make is slightly harder to play than the more streamlined G.M. that doesn't seem to be the case.

On the downside, it is wood, and I've heard wood harps can have swelling problems. Also, the construction doesn't seem quite as robust as the G.M. For example the screws are smaller and will require a really small driver to remove (there's 4 on his one, while the G.M. has two). However, it's a quality harp and the differences really are minor.

Everyone I talk to always says the Marine Band is the best harp for under $50, now I know why. It's a great harp for any newbie, or like me, a someone who's been a beginner for a few years.

product_title: Emerson GM527 Karaoke Player with 7-inch LCD Screen, DVD/CDG/MP3G/iPod Compatibility & Voice Recording
review_headline: I had to return this product
review_body: This product could have been really great.  It has tons of functionality. You can even play MP3s from a flash drive.  However, when I would try to play a CD or a MP3, the machine would play for a few minutes then stop and go back to the beginning of the CD or track.  It would not play a CD past about the 5th song.  I didn't get a chance to try a DVD, so I'm not sure how that works.  The CDs included with the machine were just okay.  There seemed to be a lot of songs geared towards kids.  If you want to have a party with adults singing karaoke, I would definitely search for other karaoke CDs to purchase.  Also, the owner's manual is poorly written and doesn't talk about all the options on the machine.    I unfortunately had to return this karaoke machine.  I am not sure if I just got a dud or what.  It would be worth buying another if I knew it would work properly.

product_title: Latin Percussion CP376 6-Inch Tambourine With Head Single Row
review_body: Bought this for my toddler granddaughter because she likes percussion toys..she loves it and plays with it constantly. It arrived on time and was just as advertized.

product_title: World Tour Deluxe Padded Keyboard Bench
review_body: so it may not look as nice as some of the more furniture type benches, but it sure feels great, sturdy, firm padding. Don't let the \\"off brand\\" discourage you. I read the many negative yamaha bench reviews and was a bit leery of a brand i never heard of. But boy was I wrong. No need to worry. great product.

product_title: Tascam PSP520 AC  Adapter/Power Supply For Mpgt1
review_body: If you are thinking to buy this AC adapter to use with Tascam DR-05, forget about it. I was persuaded by Amazon to buy both together, as both are shown in the section \\"Frequently Bought Together\\", but this is a bad mistake (and Amazon didn't fix it yet; on 08/21/2011 still shows the pair: [...])! I returned it (from Brazil), explaining this misfortune, and they did the reimbursement. What a shame Amazon!

product_title: Black and White Yin/yang Ocarina/whistle/flute
review_body: This was purchased for my daughter.  I played the flute in my high school marching band.  Ocarinas are dear to my heart.  My daughter plays percussion in the high school band.  She loves this ocarina.  She has been playing tunes for us ever since she opened it on Christmas day.  Thanks so very much for this Yin/yang ocarina!!!

product_title: Meinl Percussion DDG1-BK Bamboo Didgeridoo - Black
review_body: I bought this didgeridu for my sister for Christmas, sort of as a ongoing joke - I buy her an unusual instrument every year - who would have known that she had already had a didgeridu, but it had a crack in it and was unplayable... THIS one however was perfect!!  It came in perfect condition - no cracks, wonderful design.  She was able to play it right away and was completely satisfied with the sound it produced.

product_title: Guitar Foot Stool 7590
review_body: My husband finally broke his old stand that has been with him for years. This was an exact replacement for the old one and he is a happy camper. Sturdy and durable.

product_title: D'Addario EJ46-3D Pro-Arte Nylon Classical Guitar Strings, Hard Tension, 3 Sets
review_body: I Imagine that if I were to string my guitar with cooked spaghetti it would sound exactly like these strings. The trebles are muddy and snappy and the bass is to brassy with not enough low end. Perhaps Daddario's composite strings are more reliable but I don't recommend these if you are a tone junkie like me.

product_title: DW Drum Workshop 3000 SERIES DWCP3100 THRONE W/ VISE MEMORY
review_body: Solid throne.  I've owned it for one month and have not had any problems.  Locking seat height is reliable and does not slip, I'm 6' and 220 lbs..  Seat is comfortable.  I've noted a slight squeak recently, but nothing WD-40 cannot solve.

product_title: Bow-Right for 1/4 - 1/2 Violin - Teaching Tool and Training Accessory
review_headline: Works okay when it's on but a pain to use overall
review_body: My daughter takes violin lessons and her violin teacher suggested we purchased a bow guard/guide to help her strenghten her wrist motion and teach her how to keep the bow nice and straight as it was swerving a bit.    The idea itself is great...the actual use of it...it is not.  For starters, there is no way that a six year old can put this tool on or off by herself. I had to do it for her each time and trust me, there was some frustration on my part associated with the process, which took several minutes.  The problem is that you have to open the sides wide enough to fit the width of the instrument by stretching the metal bars yet retaining the same shape.  This is very tricky.  I don't know how anyone can do this without scratching the violin. Everytime I had to do this I would cringe wondering of the damage this would cause the violin.  If that wasn't bad enough, even once it was on it kept moving and sliding proving little worth to what we are actually trying to do: keep her bow straight and in line.    Finally although it did help a bit, more than often she slid her bow right through the metal bars making me cringe, once more,as the bow could easily be broken or damaged this way.  I have heard the pencil trick by placing them in the sound holes.  We had some concerns about this because I heard that it can ruin the violin and actually distort the sound.  All in all: only use this for a few weeks, and be VERY careful with it.

product_title: Odyssey LATSA2 Speaker Mount Tripod Accessory
review_headline: IMHO ... its OK ... But there is a better product on this site
review_body: This unit is quite functional as is and even comes with screws to facilitate mounting. I received my order well in advance of the estimated due date and in excellent condition. I would be more satisfied with it if it weren't for the fact that I also ordered a similar product from a different seller and manufacturer on Amazon which seems superior in construction and material than this one. Its just my own personal preference and observation after comparing the two units side by side. I liked the deeper seating, solid weight, heavier duty feel, the welded joints, the smoother professional finish and the counter-sunk mounting holes of the other unit so much so that I re-ordered more from the other seller and am keeping these as backups.

product_title: Pedaltrain Pro With Soft Case
review_body: No complains about the pedalboard. USeful and good price ($121 I paid). What sucks is that Amazon keeps using UPS. They didn't leave the thing at my door, even when I left a long letter asking them to do it and making myself responsible if anything would happen to the package. I called them to pick it up (I needed it that evening, that's why I paid more for the rush order). They told me the truck driver would not arrive on time for the customer pick-up are to be open. ?!?!? I hate UPS.

product_title: Seiko SQ50-V Quartz Metronome Packs
review_body: I bought the metronome to use in Spinning classes.  It's easy to change bpm and visible to class participants.  The only negative I have found is the 4 bpm range between settings.

product_title: Meinl Percussion DDG1-BK Bamboo Didgeridoo - Black
review_body: This may not be the most expensive instrument, but for a beginner it is just fine.  I bought this because I have sleep apnea and there was a recent German study which noted improvement in people after six months of daily half-hour sessions didgeridooing.  You really have to buy a book of instructions with the instrument so that you can have full benefit.  Oddly, even though it is a wind instrument, it has aspects which remind you of percussion.  Didgeridoos range all the way up in price to the thousands of dollars if made by native Australians...so this is just fine for me.  Of course, if they ask me to play at Carnegie Hall, I will consider a more costly toot.

product_title: SANOXY FM Transmitter /Car Charger/ Holder
review_body: This is really affordable and it gets about the same reception/quality as the $65+ Belkin fm transmitter for my Ipod touch 2g. The only thing is that since it's so cheap, it also breaks really easily. I bought this exact one about a year ago and it just recently broke. The part that is inserted into the ipod/iphone bends and breaks off really easily so handle with care. I had this fm transmitter connected to my ipod and I left it resting in a cupholder between the driver and front passenger seat. When I reached over and down to pick up a water bottle from the floor of the front passenger seat (don't worry, I was parked), my body nudged the fm transmitter and it broke off from the ipod and is, of course, unusable). Even with this awareness, I still think this is a better buy than the name brand kind because those aren't fool proof either (the wiring came loose within a year) and this generic one is way cheaper.     P.S. If you have a hard case on your ipod I highly recommend you get one with a large, wide opening at the bottom because if you have a hard case with an opening that's just wide enough for the connecting region then the fm transmitter can't be inserted to completely fit all the way (hopefully I'm making sense). I used to have a really cheap one dollar clear acrylic hard case for my ipod touch and the fm transmitter would become loose really easily and lose reception when connected but since I switched over to a speck candy shell case with an opening at the bottom that spans practically the width of the ipod I haven't had any problems.

product_title: Evans Genera HD Dry Drum Head
review_body:
this snare head is amazing

its so easy to tune you basically are just tighteneing it down the first time until you happy and it sounds great

and not to mention how good it sounds, alot warmer than my previous snare head and sounds so much better

product_title: Kona Acoustic Guitar Starter Pack For Dummiesar
review_body: We bought this for my sister who was just thinking about playing a guitar.  We figured why go out and buy something really expensive off the bat when we could buy her this.  The sound from the guitar is what you would expect from a cheap guitar, but honestly it was not that bad.  It was a very good guitar to learn on, and she has since upgraded to one of the more expensive guitars.  I think that this helped her learn how to play, so this gets five stars from me!

product_title: Dunlop Tortex Jazz Guitar Picks
review_body: The reasons I like this pick include:  The shape: I like jazz picks. They are big enough to hold on to. And, small enough to palm for fingerstyle work.  The texture: The surface is rough enough to hold onto. Yet, it does not give a harsh top end to the attack.  Thickness: It is thick enough for good lead playing. But, not so stiff that it is impossible to strum.  Tone: Every pick adds sonic characteristics to your playing. This pick is the closest to my snapping technique and provides a smooth transition between my different articulation methods.

product_title: On Stage RS7500 Tiltback Amplifier Stand
review_body: In the past I'd bought similar stands, and they'd usually break right at the neck in about a year. This stand, I was impressed the moment it was removed from the box. Of immediate note was the superior construction. It handles my large 80 pound 2x12 combo amp with ease. It also folds up to be very portable, enough to fit in the back of the amp while traveling. Wish I found this stand many years ago.

product_title: SANOXY FM Transmitter /Car Charger/ Holder
review_headline: Not bad for the price; not a great device, though
review_body:
I use this device with an iPhone 4. I connect it to the iPhone and it does transmit on the selected frequency. Sound quality is about as good as an FM transmission device like this gets. That is to say it's quite usable, but wouldn't be mistaken for a CD or \\"real\\" FM radio.

The device itself is a little flimsy, kind of cheaply made. That isn't a shock, given the price I paid for it. However, one irritating thing about it is that the connection is \\"fussy\\" and slips out too easily. It has to be perched \\"just so\\" in order to maintain the connection.

Also, if I'm running a video (don't worry, I don't watch them while driving), I sometimes get an alert that the attached device does not support charging. The device does not in fact charge the phone, I left it on all night and it gained no charge at all.

ADDENDUM: the seller saw my weak review of this product and refunded my money fully, without requiring me to ship it back. I can still complain about the product, but the seller is a stand-up guy.

product_title: Everest EZ Series Shoulder Rest for 4/4 - 3/4 Violin
review_headline: Excellent shoulder rest at a great price
review_body: I am extremely happy with this product. I own several shoulder rests, and this quickly became my favorite and stays on my favorite violin. I have no problem whatsoever keeping it on the violin as long as it's in the proper position. The adjustability is a key factor, and I can turn one side low and the other side higher for a highly customized fit. The padding is also excellent and comfortable. A top-quality product.

product_title: Hal Leonard 50 Licks Rock Style DVD
review_headline: Solid lessons and a great value
review_body: For less than the price of one guitar lesson you get video instruction for 50 licks.  Tom does a good job demonstrating how to play each lick and explaining what scale and key it comes from.  He plays the lick at normal speed, breaks it down in phrases, plays the complete lick slow and then finishes at full speed again with a rhythm section.    The licks are mostly classic rock with a few tasty rockabilly gems thrown in.  I would say that this is DVD is for the intermediate level of guitar player and is not for new players, but perhaps an \\"advanced beginner\\" could navigate a select few and learn more over time.    The DVD also comes with Tabs.  Between watching and listening I have no problem learning the licks and haven't had to refer to the tabs, but it is nice to have it just for clarification purposes.    The only criticism I have is that the guitar recording is a bit quiet compared to the instructors voice.    But for 10 bones I can't and won't complain.    An Excellent Value!

product_title: Shure PG2/PG58 Handheld Transmitter M7
review_headline: Don't buy it online unless you know how to setup the frequency
review_body: I got the Shure PG2/PG58 Handheld Transmitter M7. The device didn't work at all with my shure receiver (PG288/PG58). I tought it was the transmitter that it was broken since my 2 lavaliers were working fine. I sent it back and I got my refund, no problems at all. After contacting a local store they asked me to take the receiver to the store for checking the device operation frequency. I was told the transmitter must be setup with the same frequency as the receiver and shure company is the one who setup those devices. That's why the handheld transmitter didn't work with my receiver. If you know how to setup the frequency for the handheld transmitter get it online. I think sellers of this device should know about this matter and they should advice online customers about it. No sense at all to sell an item that is going to be send it back.

product_title: Oscar Schmidt OU5 Concert Ukulele
review_body: When I decided on the Oscar Schmidt OU5 Concert Koa Ukulele, my only apprehension was the distance the order had to travel - I live in Canberra, Australia. My order, placed through Springdale Music in Chardon, Ohio (via Amazon), arrived well within its estimated delivery time. Although the outer packaging sustained some damage (as I had worried it would), I was relieved to find the ukulele survived unscathed. The order was definitely well packaged. The OU5 was in its own separate box surrounded by air pillows within another larger box. Springdale Music has certainly put in the extra effort to ensure the ukulele would survive the long journey. THIS SHOULD BE AN IMPORTANT CONSIDERATION FOR OVERSEAS BUYERS. I am a very happy customer, to say the least. The OU5 is exceptionally beautiful and well-made. It has an antiqued old world charm about it. When I first read that the OU5 is made in Indonesia, I took comfort from the fact that good Indonesian craftsmen - if Oscar Schmidt were to use them - can be very good indeed. Highly recommended item and seller.

product_title: 9 Pack Planet Waves Classic Series Instrument Cable with Right Angle Plug, 0.5 feet
review_body: Bought it after read reviews. I had signal loss using these cables.. it's like having a loose connection inside the cable. My connections were on and off, I thought I had a dead pedal.. I have to wiggle and hold to get signal. It's too flexible almost like Twizzlers (no kidding!). If you want a cheap and reliable pedal cables, go get the one from Pro Co, I bought it very cheap from Sweetwater on Ebay, surprisingly very good quality and looks durable!

product_title: Sony MDR7506 Professional Large Diaphragm Headphone
review_body:
After very little total use I am looking for my third pair of pads in three years at a cost of $25 a set ($75 and counting). My old Sennheiser headphones/pads (that I still have) lasted 25 years! I only use them for watching Blu-Ray movies when the wife is asleep. They stay in a cabinet in a velvet bag. Pads started flaking off... I will (god only knows) maybe have to buy 10 more pairs in the future? Rrrrr... notice on Amazon replacement pads are bought really OFTEN... crazy. Sony products are beautiful, but have a two year life span due to poor durability. If you are a fan of Sony products then fine, I was too. But two close friends who bought these on my recommendation have had the exact problem. Both also walked around work with black specks stuck to their faces not knowing what the source was...

***UPDATE*** Please read the review of this Sony products' earcups at the following competitors' earcup replacements have been used by a dozen other owners (a suitable replacement there) at Beyerdynamic EDT 200 ear cushions. They state the problem better then I can... these Sony cups will disintegrate within a year's time (or two etc.). I bought a set of those new velour ones and am VERY happy almost two years now. Thanks folks for the kind update (those of you have expressed discontent at other forum members bringing up a valid and established issue are way off base! ... please just let the 'easy fix' be published instead of comment on your 'feelings' on hundred dollar headphones needing almost immediate replacement) ... take care all you wonderful other Amazon update people who have helped and assisted with this issue!

UPDATE June/2014 ... The left channel went out on these earphones long ago, binned. I have since purchased Grado, have not looked back once. I have disabled ALL Amazon alerts, so to those of you sane persons... best of luck with your purchase. To any of those who would state that their feelings about a product are superior to others, my wife says: these men were abused as children, are still children, have never truly experienced love... we should pray for them... and be thankful someone else has to wipe up all the venomous spittle. *whew*

product_title: SX RST White Left Handed Guitar Package w/GA1065
review_body: I got all the items exactly as advertised, in good condition and on time.    I'm just starting to learn how to play the guitar and I feel this is a good enough package that comes with everything you need to get started!  The guitar feels and sounds great.  I found the instructional DVD quite helpful, even if it was for right-handed students, I could mirror the techniques on my left-handed guitar.  The amp is decent enough - yes, there is a slight 'buzz' as described by another reviewer, but it can be reduced by lowering the volume or moving farther from the amp.    All in all, a good purchase. I would recommend it to anyone who wants to explore and learn to play an electric guitar, but is wary of spending too much the first time.

product_title: SKB Thin-Line Classical Guitar Soft Case
review_headline: so far best blend of portability and protection
review_body:
Perfect fit for my Yamaha APX500 II.
Stable inside, sturdy outside, convenient side handle and backpack straps.
Zipper is strong --- gets a bit stuck zipping and unzipping but not a major enough problem to be a con.

product_title: SANOXY FM Transmitter /Car Charger/ Holder
review_body:
I got this for my husband as a Christmas present. Tested this out before hand and it came through crisp and clear. It works better on channels with static, I live out in the country so there's plenty of that. But if you live in a large city then I image you would have probems finding a god clear/static-filled channel for this device.

On another note: I have bought transmitters like this before for other devices and have discovered that after regular hard use of them they begin to burn out eventually and finally kick the bucket. I wouldn't call this just one manufacturer default. From what I've read, the same thing happens with all types and all brands. So you're best to find one that YOU, the buyer likes at a decent price and buy two. That way when it finally does burn out you have your back-up. I'll be amazed if this thing lasts a month and longer. When I read the reviews, I was looking for the quality of sound through this product. Not reading to see how many times it will burn out.

All-in-all, this and every other brand WILL burn out/break over time. But for this price, with the good quality of sound in your radio. Buy this product. If you want to try it out then I suggest just one, just to see if it's right for you. But to others whome have had products like this before, buy two so you have your back-up.

product_title: Pacific Drums and Percussion 700 Series Drum Throne
review_headline: You can NOT beat this throne for the price
review_body: I have found this throne to be comfortable for studio use and it seems to be solid enough for everyday use.  It is sturdy and heavy enough for the average player and the price is definitely right.  The padding is just about right and feels good and comfortable for the session times for which I have used it.  I don't know how it would hold up for touring or constant use, but it is perfect for my needs, as I am a guitarist who plays drums for demos in the studio.

product_title: Yamaha Arius YDP-V240 88-Key Digital Piano,
review_body:
Here is a review from the perspective of an adult beginner: I'm very happy with my Yamaha Arius YDPV240. I am a beginner at piano (in my late 40's) as is my 6 year old daughter. We've had the piano for about six months. I did not buy the piano from Amazon, but purchased from Kraft Music.

Before I started playing piano six months ago, I thought there was not any real difference between a digital and acoustic instruments except for the modern conveniences. However, I must say that whenever I am able to play a \\"real\\" piano I find the differences quite stunning. In fact, when I see an acoustic piano I do my best to sit down and play it if I can! Real pianos have a wide variety of \\"touches\\"--some are much stiffer, some less so, and getting notes to sound is different than on my Yamaha digital piano. Also, acoustic pianos are full of strings, of course, and these strings VIBRATE, and that vibration comes through strongly in the keys and can be felt with the fingers and also with the body. This is a very different feeling. Experiencing these things makes me also want an acoustic piano, and realize that if I really had the $$$ the thing to get would be a Yamaha Disklavier, which is an acoustic piano and digital piano in the same instrument. Maybe some day ...

Back to the Yamaha Arius YDPV240. I am happy with my purchase. It was a reasonable amount to spend, but I know we will enjoy this for years. I love being able to practice with headphones when my children are sleeping, and to be able to control the volume when not using headphones. Acoustic pianos are VERY LOUD. It's nice that the digital piano does not have to be. However, if I turn it up to maximum volume, the volume feels like that of a real acoustic piano. I also love being able to record what I play and play it back. This is nice for practicing, as it forces me to find a tempo where I can play my piece through without mistakes. And it is nice to be able to listen to myself more objectively (than I can when playing at the same time). My daughter very much enjoys having the different instrument \\"voices.\\" She will play with a variety of voices during her practice sessions and when she is fooling around. I think it is a lot of fun for her. She's taking conventional lessons, but I also teach her what I'm learning with the \\"Simply Music\\" method. She fools around with the Simply Music pieces quite a bit, playing them in different positions on the piano and it is interesting that when she transposes to a minor key she will choose a \\"spooky\\" sounding organ, for example. It's also fun to be able to play baroque music using the harpsichord, etc. I like the different expressive options one has with the digital piano--it is many instruments in one, in a sense.

My main disappointment with this piano was the bench. It is too small to accommodate me and my daughter to play four-handed piano. I just bought a new bench (see my review of the piano bench I just bought, Griffin's \\"Ebony Black Leather Piano Bench Wood Double Duet Keyboard Seat with Storage\\") so that we can more comfortably play together. I wish Yamaha provided bench options, as a storage bench that seats two seems to make sense to me!

I'm glad to recommend this piano!

product_title: Gtd-Audio 2 x 300Watt 8 Channel Audio Powered Mixer
review_headline: Worked Great ... Then Died After Just 20 Hrs Of Use
review_body:
INITIAL REVIEW: I ordered a GTD Audio model BM-9100 8 channel 600W powered audio mixer which I received earlier than expected and tested it as soon as I unpacked it. I was pleased with both the timely delivery and the performance of the powered pre-amp. I hooked it up to two pairs of the Pro Audio Monitor 1200Cs that I ordered and had arrived at about the same time. I was very impressed at the quality, workmanship, clarity, volume and power of the unit which includes a built-in 7 band graphic equalizer aside from the simpler tone control for highs and lows provided with each of the 8 channel inputs. Along with the stereo power output led indicators, the unit uses two separate master volume controls, one for each of the two stereo output channels (A/B) and a control for the record playback volume. I am by no means a professional DJ or have experience in using this type of professional equipment, but I decided on its purchase after experiencing problems re-cabling the stage equipment that had been in use the night previously provided by a local social club that I belong to. Even without reading the sparse instructions, the well placed dials and plugins were clearly labeled and their used intuitive for those with some home audio equipment knowledge, with one exception ... the use and settings for the special audio effects. Here is where additional instructions in the included manual would have been much appreciated, as is the lack of a list of functional labels to compliment the numerical digital effects selector. Maybe I'll be lucky enough to find someone to explain the use of this function to me or find instructions somewhere online. For the price ... if this equipment holds up ... it definitely seems like a decent buy.

FOLLOW UP REVIEW (May 6, 2012): My unit is DEAD!!! The unit began to smoke and burn while in use yesterday morning. I haven't a clue as to why?!!! I must have used it no more than 5 times and a total of 20 hours. What's more ... I have never ever maxed it out ... I've been careful not to push it beyond a quarter of its capable output. Its always been a pampered piece of my equipment collection and have always carefully packed it away between uses. Upon reviewing my initial comments about the unit, I was surprised to find a photo of another model posted on site which I don't recognize. If the difference is merely cosmetic \\"Buyer Beware.\\" As of yet, I don't know what options I may have for repairing or replacing this mixer. I can't seem to get a hold of the manufacturer via the web url. As of now, all I can do is readjust my rating. I am very disappointed with what happened.

product_title: Shure E500PTH Sound Isolating Earphones
review_headline: Outstanding except for one minor flaw
review_body: I ordered a pair of these back in early '08 during an overseas deployment. Since then they have endured three other deployments, countless other trips, and Lord-only-knows how many hours of use thanks to my laptop, iPod and PSP. The sound isolation is excellent (almost good enough to drown out the engine noise of a C-130 and easily able to block out the engine noise of a KC-135, which I always fly on). Even on these planes I only need my electronics turned up a couple notches from completely silent, as opposed to my old Bose QuietComfort headset, which I had to have everything nearly maxed out for volume when flying. Suffice it to say I fully believe that canal style headphones can very likely prevent or postpone tinnitus or hearing loss when used in environments like mine. I don't have to crank up the audio to drown out outside noise. Someone has to come up and physically get my attention or else I simply will not hear them; even when I have no audio playing through them. They are so comfortable I can easily fall asleep on a plane with them still in and not be bothered at all. Sound quality as well is phenomenal. High notes are pristine, mids are perfect and not distracting, and bass is much more firm and crisp than even the Sony Studio Monitor and the Bose QuietComfort headphones I used to own. I even compared them to a friend's full size Sennheiser headset, and the Shure phones won hands-down. Even he agreed that these sounded far better. On the downside to the audio quality though: they will show any and all flaws in the source audio because their reproduction is so accurate. It's just like how a CD will show the flaws of a poor analog recording, or a BluRay disc will show flaws in the video that weren't noticed on DVD or VHS.    Now that I've covered the positives though, I should mention the one negative of the Shure brand of canal phones: no replaceable cord. After three years of intensive use (which, granted is a long time, and I have used them a LOT), the insulation on my cords where they pass over the ears has become brittle and finally broken, taking very fine wiring with it. Obviously they're way out of warranty by now and I'd have to pay to have them repaired, if they even can be. My next earphones will be a higher end set from Ultimate Ears, since they offer replacement cables. I can only hope they sound as good as my Shures have.    If you're buying for light use, I wouldn't hesitate to get these. But if you're going to be putting your headphones through the life I've given mine, I'd strongly recommend finding a pair with a replaceable cord.

My only complaints are that it won't stay in my bell for long without my left hand to hold it and the stem won't stay in the mute either. product_title: Rode VideoMic Pro Compact VMP Shotgun Microphone
review_headline: Cheap build quality for the price
review_body:
This has quite cheap build quality for the price. The cord on it is almost a joke and it's not a question of if it will break, but when. For the price charged, this microphone is overpriced given the low build quality and no 9V battery included in the box.

Audio performance-wise, it's still best to get as close to the subject as possible for the best audio. You need to be within 6 feet from this mic or you are not going to be able to achieve professional sounding results using this mic across the room or anything like that. There is just too much room echo/ambient noise. That said, this is better than the built in mic on most cameras so it's not bad if you are close to it in a small room for example, or to get environmental or background audio out in the field.

If you attach it to a boom pole so you can get it close to the subject, it can effectively be used for filmmaking productions. Rode does sell an extension cable which seems of pretty good quality for a good price.

If you do talking head type videos or product reviews, a lavalier mic would probably suit you better.

This mic does have a relatively small size which is quite convenient.
