review_body: I ordered this light for a large dance event we were having.  It was out in the country and i actualy mounted this product on a tree and aimed it down on the dancefloor.  It worked perfectly.  I love this product and i actualy have it mounted on my living room wall now.  It is not a huge clunky light and is perfect for large events or just making your own party at home.  I'm sure people driving up and down our street some nights wonder what is going on at our house when I turn it on crank up the music and me and my 4 yr old have our own dance party!  It is great and has different settings.  I like the setting that moves the lights to the sound of the music.  I would recommend it to anyone who likes lighting as much as i do.  If you are d.j. it is a great travel size light.

product_title: Casio PX-110 Privia Digital Piano
review_body: Overall I am very happy with this keyboard - it's great for getting the feel of a grand piano in a small space for a relatively small price.  It is the most reasonably priced digital piano with weighted keys I could find anywhere.  I am not that experienced but to me the keys feel very much like a grand piano.  The sound is not great through the built in speakers (and the keys are somewhat noisy), but is actually quite realistic through headphones.    According to a friend it works well as a midi controller, too (he uses a mac and garageband).  I have not tried this, but he gets outstanding sound out of it this way.

product_title: Cecilio CEVN Style 1 Silent Electric Solid Wood Violin with Ebony Fittings
review_body: And it's not just the looks, this electric violin sounds surprisingly good when using headphones or amplifier. The bow is nice. It definitely needs a shoulder rest, some better rosin and a better set of strings, but for the price, this is wonderful. The line out jack does not seem to work (or I couldn't figure it out), but the phones jack works just fine for the amp. The price was even better after google'ing it ;) Nice as a gift to my dad.

product_title: Korg EMX1 Electribe MX Music Production Station
review_headline: Learn To Love It And It Will Love You!
review_body: You will not find a more fun groove box on the market for this type of money, trust me. Debated whether to get this or the ESX, and SO glad i picked this one.  Picked up a Roland SP-404 as a sampler instead, and the two work flawlessly together.  The great thing about this box is definitely the versatility, you can program beats on it, perform live, use it with a MIDI controller, or route your audio thru it as a signal processor.  The possibilities are basically endless, and once you start making your own sounds, you can pretty much delete the presets and add even more functionality.  The best thing to come along for bedroom producers since the SH-101.  No regrets.

product_title: Edirol FA-66 6 x 6 FireWire Audio Interface
review_headline: this BRICK works best with Texas Instruments 1394 controller on-board.
review_body: do not expect this to work unless you have a texas instruments firewire card built in to your computer.  pretty much, only buy this if you are using a mac.  otherwise its snap crackle and pop world for the rest of your life right before you end it due to extreme frustration.      this is my experience under vista and on a DELL p.o.s. laptop that i thought would be technologically mature enough to 'hang' with pro audio.  I was wrong.  this is just one small part of a big costly lesson that i am learning in my life.  no matter how much research i seem to do in any subject, it never seems to be enough until i bang my head hard and with tenacity against that proverbial wall.    if i could rate this product again i would give it a zero because i would have to buy a whole different computer to get it to work.  goodbye cruel world.    i mistakenly thought an expresscard firewire 'band aid' would make my p.o.s. Dell 1710 inspiron play nice with the FA-66.      THERE IS NO WAY this thing will function in any meaningful capacity at 192khz sample rates.  Not unless you are using a CRAY supercomputer.  or a mac, as many will profess.  You are talking sonic meltdown within seconds, as this overpriced and poorly implemented interface takes you down with it.  what does aluminum go for by the pound these days?    Not happy with this brick.

product_title: Roosebeck Plastic Practice Chanter Reed w/ Copper Staple
review_body: At this point, we've all been told that most of the piping-related goods coming out of Pakistan are of poor quality. Ok, this is usually true. However, in my experience, I've have used these reeds quite often from the early days of starting out to the days of playing in Grade one. More money will often buy you better reeds, but honestly, I've played reeds like these in every type of chanter, and they generally work acceptably well. In one of my best chanters, I've had a Pakistani reed in there for at least eight years and never had trouble with it. A reed being of a known brand name DOES NOT mean that it's better than everything else. Many Pakistani practice chanter reeds can be quite good. It's just better to have a few to choose from, and what's wrong with having an extra reed or two anyway?

product_title: Breedlove Atlas Series AD25/SR Plus Acoustic Electric
review_headline: An excellent underrated piece of instrument
review_body: I bought one of these back in April, 2007 and I have fallen in love with them ever since.  I have been playing for over 30+ years and have owned other brand name guitars (electics and acoustics), and this one has been one favorite of mine ever since.    The body is tremendous.  Its heavy, but the neck is flat and very playable.  The balance of sound is amazing, especially for the price.  The built-in Fishman 4T tuner is a godsend, and the hard shell case that came with it is first class.  There are no words to describe the feeling that I get everytime I strum and I hear either high or low notes reverberate with so much clarity - no muddiness like the Martins, no over-brightness like the Taylors, and certainly not cheap like the Yamahas.    This guitar is a keeper with its beautiful abalone inlays. The proprietary JLD truss under the bridge creates that balanced sound even with the thin upper wood.  The Grover tuners are easy and mine does not require a whole of lot of tuning.  Make sure to get the best humidifier to protect this amazing guitar.  Try one at any of the big name guitar stores (GC?) and you'll know what I'm talking about.  I was going to get a Martin or a Taylor and this baby blew them all away.

product_title: Ion iCD04FX Personal Audio Portable DJ Station
review_body: I return it the next day. It didn't work, the sound was not clear at all. Save you money the sale is not a sale if the product don't work.

product_title: Echo Indigo IO Stereo 24/96 Laptop Cardbus
review_headline: Very pleased with Echo Indigo I/O Card
review_body: Initially I had planned to buy a Creative sound card, but happened upon a good review of this card, so I took a plunge.  I have been very pleased with the card.  I have a Compaq EVO laptop that I use the card with.  I have used it to digitize my old music collection:  LPs and cassettes primarily.  I connect my old Elac Miracord 770h turntable to a Carver preamp, then the preamp out to the Indigo.  I use the Cakewalk Pyro 5 software to pull in the analog sound and then cut it into tracks.  I adjust the input volume using the preamp volume control.  As far as output from the card, I run it through a Cambridge Soundworks Model Twelve portable system.  Sounds quite good to my admittedly aging ears.  The weak link in my case is either my ears or the condition of the LPs and cassettes.  I thought about giving it a 4 because it hogs the two slots area on my laptop, but that's no real problem, just a minor annoyance.

product_title: Morley VAI-2 Steve Vai Bad Horsie 2 Contour Wah
review_body: Great pedal!  I've bought it used and it came in great condition! Just as the seller said!  Right on time!

product_title: Sennheiser  HD 202 Dynamic Headphones (Old Version)
review_body: I've had these phones for a few weeks now and have had no problems with them. They have very good sound quality, especially when you make a price\quality comparison. They come with a long cord and Sennheiser includes a cord winder so you can adjust the length to what you need. Comfort is good, even after several hours of use. I haven't had them long enough to make an estimate of how well they will hold up, but I've been using them almost every day with no issues. All in all, it's easy to recommend them without reservation.

product_title: Hosa IRG-100.5 Low-Profile Right-Angle Guitar Patch Cable, 6 inch
review_body: 6\\" is pretty short and will only work if your inputs/outputs are on the sides--too short if they are on the top. Also, it's the weirdest thing, but these 1/4\\" plugs don't work in all of my pedals. They are too big for some of them. Odd.    Merchant was great, so they get 5 stars.

product_title: Alvarez AD4104BK Artist Series Dreadnought Acoustic Guitar, Black
review_body: Great guitar for the price. Super low action and very bright sounding. Stays in tune like an expensive guitar. At $135, I don't think there's anything in that price range that can come close.

product_title: Levy's Leathers MT8M-GLD 2-inch Metallic Cotton Guitar Strap
review_body:
I love Levy's guitar straps, and this one is quality workmanship like the others (excluding the ones with the little plastic slip ring - hate those straps). The heavy cotton is super durable, much like the strap of an old canvas duffle bag that will never die. The distressed look is way cool and gives the strap character. It's even better in person. The only thing I wasn't too happy with is that the leather ends have a thickness of approximately 5mm or 6mm and make it very hard to use Schaller Strap Locks which have a thread length of 6mm or 7mm. On a Gibson Faded Special with a typical Gibson endpin, the Levy's leather/canvas is as thick as the space from the wood to the tip of the endpin. But the pins or buttons are not the issue. How this affects use of the lock mechanism is the issue. I only use the Schaller's strap locks that way I don't have to keep readjusting the strap from guitar to guitar, and I lessen the possibility of the strap slipping of the pins and the guitar plummeting to the floor. At the endpin openings on both ends, this particular Levy's strap is as thick as the threading on the Schaller lock and doesn't leave space for the washer and nut which is of course, essential to the strap not slipping off the end. If you don't use the washer, or you don't plan on using strap locks, you'll probably really like this strap, but if you want that extra security of the washer, well, so far, there hasn't been enough elbow grease or brunt force to get the washer and nut on this strap. However, I'm still hopeful (or is that stubborn?).

If I was going to use this strap, I would use the little plastic rings with the cut-outs that slide between the strap and the endpin to hold the strap on the guitar, but if you want the luxury of using Schallers so you can do a quick strap change, this strap comes up short... but it is a durable strap.

product_title: Epiphone LP Special II Les Paul Electric Guitar, Vintage Sunburst
review_body: I also bought this guitar like a Christmas present for myself. And I can say this guitar sounds great, is beautiful for me.  I can say this Les Paul is very good and I recommen to everybody

product_title: Clear Voice Vocal Spray- 1 Bottle
review_body: I bought this and the vocal eze product. I sing a wide variety of songs, from raspy rock to clean smooth styles. I suffer from spring alergies and was hoping this could get me through the rough spots. I actually lost vocal range with this stuff and couldn't get the normal growl in my voice for the rock tunes. It was awful. It could be that the throat issues were alergy driven, but this stuff was supposed to help. I will not buy it again. One good thing is that it tasted pretty good so if you are more interested in nice flavour rather than results, its not bad.

product_title: Mackie PROFX8 8-Channel Mixer
review_body: I had high hopes for the Mackie Profx8 based on the great feature set.  Has everything in features that I want in a compact mixer.  Hooked it up and first show went great.  I'd say sound quality was excellent.  Much better than the Alesis multimix 8 that I was replacing.  Effects were so so but useable.  Build quality seemed ok, but didn't knock my socks off.  Unfortunately, in the second use one of the stereo channels went out. I baby my equipment so I'm sure that it wasn't knocked around or roughly handled. Based on other reviews regarding noise in using the usb recording, and fears about the quality, I elected to send back and not replace with the same model.  Replacing with an Allen & Heath Zed 10fx.  To be seen if better quality can be had at this price point.

product_title: 10" Professional Double-Row Tunable Tambourine Wood
review_body: Don't think this is an A-1 sort of hand thwacker, as it is rather cheap plastic on the head, but that can be replaced when needed for almost nada. Mine had a scratch in the plastic, but I sure can make it thump good with a wide variety of sounds and tones. The tuning is a bit loose, and the head bends the sound a bit when pressed. However, It is an acceptable hand trainer to the uninitiated and the impromptu musician's get-together whims.

product_title: Sterling Audio St55 Large Diaphragm Fet Condenser Microphone
review_body: I had read a review about the ST51 in Electronic Musician [...]and when I was researching the ST51 online I came across the ST55.  I decided to go with the ST55 only because it has the additional features of the high pass filter and attenuation pad switches.  Being a home studio I don't have the luxury of a vocal booth.  For vocal recording I use a makeshift one out of a couple mics boom stands and a duvet to make a corner for the singer to stand in front of.  The high pass filter should help the mic ignore some of the more mundane sounds of the room like the PC fan running, etc.    In addition to the mic I would highly recommend getting the shock mount and the pop-filter.  I added these accessories not because it was recommended but because they are necessities.  They help filter out unwanted noises and greatly improve the sound quality.  And when recording vocals the pop-filter helps keep the singer from trying to eat the mic :-)

product_title: TC-Helicon VoiceWorks Vocal Effects Processors
review_body: If you want to sound like a weird robot, like something out of the Outer Limits when your up on stage, this is the thing for you!  I tried all the settings I could on this and none of them improved my voice.  I had multiple choices of weird, strange, bizarre effects but that's not what I was looking for.  I wanted something that made my voice sound BETTER, not WORSE.  Is that too much to ask?  Save your time and money.  Try something else.

product_title: Seiko DM50S Clip Digital Metronome (Silver)
review_body: I use this metronome for cadence while running or bike riding. Just clip it on my cap, set the right volume and done. Perfect for my specific applications. I've had it for over a year and the original battery is still ticking. Use it 5/6 hours a week.

product_title: On Stage FS7850B Guitar Foot Rest
review_body: I broke my right shoulder in the early 80s and it became somewhat arthritic over time. Prolonged guitar practice was giving me tremendous arm pain (it actually felt like someone was taking a sledgehammer to my upper arm bone...the doctor said it was inflammation at the insertion point of tendon to muscle.  I actually stopped playing for many months because of a frozen shoulder. During the downtime that I had to endure months of physical therapy to \\"unfreeze\\" my shoulder, I studied Jamie Andreas' Guitar Principles book. I made the connection that bad posture + upper body tension = shoulder pain!!! If you are prone to shoulder pain, then playing in the \\"classical position\\" forces your right shoulder down (assuming you're a right-handed picker) and your arm will be in a more relaxed position for playing. You'll still have to monitor your arms and shoulders for any tension that might slowly creep in, but holding the guitar in the classical position, with your left foot resting on a stool such as this one will allow you to practice in a more comfortable way. It took a while to get used to sitting like this (with the guitar between my legs) and yes, I had to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous comments from my family, but I wouldn't practice any other way now! I'm nowhere near being a virtuoso yet, and I may never achieve virtuosity in this lifetime. I'm just happy that I've found a comfortable way to practice the tunes I love. That's all that really matters anyway.     I definitely recommend this foot stool!!!

product_title: Bellafina Luxolite Violin Case 4/4 Size
review_body: its a perfect case for the price. We bought it for our son who travels with his school violin. The case gets beaten up by the bus travel almost everyday. This is not the case that carries his best violin...its something for kids to take to school with their second best violin. If you have an expensive violin then this is not the case for it...comparing it to our other case...which is 4 times the cost...this is more lighter,not strong enough. look wise they both look almost the same.

product_title: Korg MA30 Ultra Compact Digital Metronome
review_body: This is a great compact metronome. Easy to use...There are several rhythmic options for subdividing the beat, an octave chromatic scale for tuning that may be adjusted to 'Baroque' pitch if you need it or higher  [Some instruments, flutes in particular are being tuned to A-442.] There is a volume control and what I like is its ability to move up or down 1 digit at a time.  The 'old' metronome moves in increments of '2', '4' & '6'.  I have recommended this metronome to my students and they are also happy with it.

product_title: ADJUSTRITE Musician's Chair by Vivo USA
review_headline: JUST WHAT I WAS LOOKING FOR
review_body: I play acoustic guitar sitting down and do about 50 gigs a year.  It seems like there is never a decent chair in the coffee houses and other venues I play in to use.  They're either really uncomfortable or so rickety I think they're going to fall over at any time.  I have been looking for something for a long time that is comfortable, portable, and reasonably priced.  Stools just don't cut it and everything in a chair I've looked at over the years has been heavy, non collapsible, or so expensive I could practically buy another guitar with what they cost. This thing is great!  At $159 it is extremely reasonable.  It is also very comfortable and has a lot of adjustability and feels VERY solid.  And, it folds up like a simple folding auditorium chair you'd see almost anywhere so it takes up very little space when I'm packing for a gig.  It certainly would also work well for cello, violin and other players who sit while playing.  I'll probably buy a second one just to have when someone sits in with me. 5 stars!!!!!

product_title: Bugera V5 5-Watt Class-A Valve Amplifier Combo with Reverb And Power Attenuator
review_body: I really like this amp for use at the house.  The power attenuator is great for cranking down the volume while still getting a natural tube sound.  I have found that I almost always run mine on the 0.1 watt setting and it's plenty loud for me in the lving room.  Sounds best when the tubes are not driven too hard (just mild distortion / tube breakdown).  If you push it too hard it gets into a king of weird tube breakdown that I'm not too crazy about, but maybe the tubes are not really broken in yet?  The built in reverb is a nice feature and has a very good sound considering it's digital.  This amp is a good deal if you just want something to get a nice bluesy tone around the house without blowing everyones ear drums out.

product_title: Vox amPlug Metal Guitar Headphone Amp
review_body: Great product. The lead tone is phenominal....some of the best I've heard ever....this includes 100 watt amps. Only complaint is the rhythm tone is kinda crunchy....more overdriven...not really distorted. But it won't bother you anyhow....I just prefer a little more gain. The battery life is pretty good, just replaced em' for the first time in 4 months of constant use. It get's pretty loud for a mini amp and if you're a diehard metal head who appreciates anything from slayer to killswitch engage...than this amp is for you.

product_title: Tacoma P1 Papoose
review_body:
This is my hundredth review, so I wanted to pick something that has given me years of joy. My whole idea in writing on amazon is that I have often appreciated finding a review I agree with on this site and then perusing the author's other reviews, and have occasionally been led to some gems I'd never heard of. So, recently I decided to just start scribbling about most of the new movies I see, and adding in some old classics from the insane numbers of books, films, and recordings I have known and loved; maybe they'll lead someone to something good.

It'll also be nice to have a list to refer to in future years to remind me what to go back and enjoy anew.
In that vein, here's the most unique guitar I've ever owned, of over a dozen.

I played and sang for a living for years, and this guitar was very useful for added texture on some of my solo and duo gigs, as well as being the ultimate portable gitbox.

I always wanted a great gitter for the beach, mountains, car, etc, but full-scale is just too big sometimes, and as I tried most of the small gits I grew weary of their poor tuners, bad set-up, wolf tones up and down the neck, and above all their tinny tone. Even if it's small, I want my guitar to give me true and pure sound, with plenty of overtones.
Enter the Papoose.

This little puppy solves the problem with a deep body and a soundhole stuck in the upper corner, letting the soundboard resonate more and thus produce more volume and tone (the soundhole does not give out sound per se; it's really a port). The Papoose is loud and full; chords are rich, with each tone distinct and clear, and the single notes are surprisingly loud; I once played this at a wedding with no mike and could be heard at the back of the loud crowd and dancers.

My Papoose was set up perfectly at the factory, with nicely rounded frets and a fast but wide neck; the tuners still rock after 9 years (I tune it down a full step to G from the tenor A it comes in, and have saved many strings from this move---the tension at the original A is rather high); and despite trashing it on many a beach and tossing it around after the initial my-honey-will-never-get-scratched period, it still plays and sounds great.

Above all, this is a MUSICAL instrument, not a toy. The Martin Backpacker plays good but sounds thin, and the Baby Taylor has the same issues, but sounds rather better. They are the only two competitors to the Papoose, but play all three one after the other, and you'll know the truth. The Papoose wins hands down, no contest.

Many thanks to the fine craftsmen and designers at Tacoma for thousands of hours of fun. I'll be buying another one soon!
Go ahead and pull out the bills because this is the travelling geetar you've always wanted. Treat yourself. You'll never regret it.

product_title: Boss ME25 Guitar Multi-Effects Pedal
review_body: First of all not having the power adapter shipped in with this was a major turn off for me. Why it has to be sold separately?! doesn't make any sense to me. The effects are alright, the individual sounds needs time to get used to it. I am currently experiencing latency coming from the USB plug (even the plug wasn't included as well).  Overall its a fun multi effect i like the loop recording ability.  The not included things were very annoying for me.

product_title: Lexicon Alpha USB Desktop Recording Studio,
review_body: Great product! I use it just for basic recording. It works well with plugging an electric guitar straight in or plugging in a mic and recording an acoustic (which is what I do). I find the CueBase program it comes with to be a bit confusing, I'm sure it's fine if you have the time to mess with all the features, but I just use Garage Band because it's very easy to use. This Lexicon works great on my Mac as well. I'm running on a PowePC (before mac went intel) and using Tiger v10.4.11. Overall I would recommend this to everyone. I haven't had a problem with it at all. Works Great!

product_title: Mighty Bright AC Adapter, 4.0V 400mA (US Adapter)
review_body: I purchased this with a mighty bright booklight.  Maybe I just got an adapter that is missing a part or something, but there is no way to connect this adapter to my mighty bright booklight which I use with my kindle, both have male plugs. There are no instructions either.  I haven't contact the company yet, but the fact that I have to do so is a bother and a black mark on them as far as I'm concerned.

product_title: CHAUVET DJ Ultimate HZ Haze Machine w/DMX Timer Remote
review_body: i like the product and use quite frequently. it does the job for me. my complaint is that is puts out alot of haze at once, so its more like a fog machine instead of putting out a continuous haze.

product_title: World Tour Deluxe Acoustic Electric Bass Guitar Gig Bag
review_body:
I have nothing but good things to say about this bag, its a great bag for the price.

Ill just add that I'm a big guy (6'4\\" 300 lbs) and this bag adjust to fit me perfectly, and also it fits my buddy (who's an average sized male) quite well.

Just word of caution for us tall people, watch the ceiling and door frames, this thing clears my head by a good 4\\"

product_title: Peavey Vypyr 75 75-Watt 1x12-Inch Combo Guitar Amplifier
review_body: This thing is absolutely what I was looking for... My trusty Johnson Marquis has seen better days, and after trying Line 6 (they make good stuff, just not their amps for me), Vox and others, I found this little gem just sitting used for $200. I snatched it, and I have gigged  (steadily) with it since! Just 1 12\\" speaker, mic it up and wail! Of course, there is a slight learning curve, but I have seen much worse. And withe stompboxes, rack fx & looper, you may never need to buy a pedal again! Do get the Sanpera II footswitch ($200 but well worth it) and a REPLACEMENT warranty plan -@ GC they sell them fairly cheap.  Overall, this thing does it all, and I was never a fan of Peavey amps, butt I am now!

product_title: Yamaha YPT400MS Portable Electronic Keyboard with  61 Full Size Touch Sensitive Keys and Keyboard Stand
review_body: Bought this keyboard to be used mainly for my 11-year old daughter who was beginning piano lessons; my other children will also use it when they are old enough. There are so many features on this piano that we've not used. I love the teaching aids and the ability to download lessons from online.  The keyboard - though portable - is well-made and has a great sound. Would definitely purchase again.

product_title: HARMONICAS 12 HARP SET - 10 HOLE EACH - EVERY KEY+ CASE
review_body: i found the box set to be rather airy, and not of very high quality. they wreaked of their carrying case and tasted like they smelled. i should have returned them immediately upon receiving them. they were too light, and didn't have a solid feeling, as well as leaking air when i played them, making it hard to play them at all. i would NEVER recommend them to anyone.

product_title: 61-KEY Portable Educational Keyboard
review_headline: YAMAHA DGX220 Keyboard is Great Fun
review_body: My DGX220 came with a power adapter and keyboard stand.  I like it's lightweight portability as I can move it myself. (We just got rid of an old, immoveable,space-eating piano we weren't using often.)  The DGX220 provides lots of other voice and instrument options and the 76 keys are plenty for me and my kids as new players.  It's a good, low cost alternative to a traditional piano if you aren't ready to make the time/money/space commitment required for something more permanent and substantial.

product_title: Singing Machine STVG-999 Pedestal Karaoke System with Tower Speakers, Camera, Monitor and Radio
review_body: I bought this as a birthday gift for my 11 year old daughter.  She and her friends used it at her birthday party much to all's delight.  We currently just use it as a stand alone, rather than plugging into the tv.  Putting it together was simple and instructions on how to use were clearly self-explanatory as the girls figured that out without adult assistance.

product_title: Musician's Friend Standard Celluloid Guitar Picks 1 Dozen Black Thin
review_body:
I tried a lot of picks, I even shaped some...
These work fine for the price, I can get THE growl on my P bass

product_title: Planet Waves Tru-Strobe Tuner
review_body: Strobe is required to tune mandolin string pairs accurately. The conventional tuners, with their */- 5 cents don't make it. This strobe is accurate within +/- 1 cent.  It will require practice to get the hang of using this tuner, but it's well worth the effort.

product_title: Peavey Vypyr 30 30-watt 1x12 Modeling Guitar Combo Amp
review_body: The amp is great but you have to have great pick-ups to get the different distortion tones. The tube screamer is kind of screachy but all the other effects are good. For $160-200 i wouldn't recommend anything else. You can come up with really any tone you want.

product_title: Rogue STR-1 Pro Electric Sitar Guitar Black with Red Crackle
review_body: I'm really impressed with this guitar. When I saw the price I thought that is was going to be a kind of \\"is worst to have nothing\\", but it turned out to be a beauty. Last month I was doing a pop production for \\"Chetes\\"and we needed something to sound like a sitar, and I didn't wanted to use synths, so we ordered it through Amazon.  Don't let it's price fool you, the guitar is noiseless, allowing you to obtain a clear and present sound. The tuning is very good, which is extremly important in recording any guitar, and the sound color is quite even throughout the scale. But the best thing is that this little thing realy sounds \\"sitarish\\". The only difficult part is tuning the resonant strings, you realy need to spend sometime tuning them, either cromaticaly or to the notes of the song, but it realy is worth the effort. This product was for me like discovering a treasure.  Potro Farias.

product_title: Casio CTK-481 Keyboard with Adapter & Song Books
review_body: I am a beginner and have not even taken my first lesson yet but I can honestly say this keyboard is pretty and looks good when I walk around with it.

product_title: Mackie 802-VLZ3 8-Ch. Compact Recording/SR Mixer
review_body: The mixer is nice and solidly built and seems to work good.  I have never  used a mixer before so some of the functions were a little confusing by reading the manual.

product_title: Rode Micro Boom Pole Telescopic Microphone Extension
review_body: Online information about this boompole is inadequate, so I thought I would write a quick first impression review.   I just purchased the Rode Mini Boompole as a handy little boom for run and gun audio. It will mainly be used with my new Tascam DR-100 portable digital recorder and external XLR mics, mostly Rode NT-4 stereo and a Sennheiser MKH 40.   My other pole is a Gitzo, but not carbon fiber. So I am working with cheap gear, not the fancier booms that full time production audio guys use.   The Rode Mini Boompole is made from aluminum tubing. It arrived with evidence of residual manufacturing oil. I wiped it down with no bad effects. I'd characterize build quality as better than a lot of indy filmmaker gear, which features a lot of improvisational engineering - dollies made with skateboard wheels and such. Machine work on locking collets is good looking and everything works well. When you disassemble the pole, as I did in an attempt to load a mic cable internally, the machine work in thread cutting is not as polished. But it is completely acceptable in a $100 item that works very well.   The Rode Mini Boompole appears large enough to feed an XLR connector internally, but this turns out not to be the case. The pole's throat is slightly too small, which appears to be a design oversight. Still, the smallest extension on the mic end of the pole is much larger than my Gitzo, which is barely large enough to thread a permanent cable before the XLR connector is affixed.   The Rode Mini Boompole does have machined channels at both ends where a permanent internal cable could be installed if desired. It also comes with velcro straps used to secure a cable externally, which is what I did when mounting my Rode NT-4 stereo mic.   I like the dense open cell hand grip material covering the entire first section of the pole. The rubber end at the base is a bit under engineered, if someone is going to rest the pole end on the ground during breaks in production. Just a flat disk of rubber less than a quarter inch. I would expect something a little more rugged and robust.   So far, I have only used the boompole in a noisy environment (high school football). Even without a suspension mount on the Rode NT-4 stereo mic, I did not notice any handling noise, even though I was listening and testing a bit. Likewise, using the supplied velcro straps to secure the mic cable externally did not seem to cause problems.   My initial reaction about weight was a bit of concern, but this turned out to be no problem, even with the largish Rode NT-4 mounted using an internal 9-volt battery in lieu of phantom power off the recorder.   In general, I enjoyed using this boompole. My application is fairly casual, no long tiresome booming. For quick sound grabbing, this is a nice addition to my kit at very low cost. I'm happy with the purchase, and would recommend it to others.  =====  UPDATE  I've had the boom a couple of years, and I like it better now than when I first got it. Why? Totally new application - running a boom camera. Running a Sony DSC-HX9V attached to the Rode Boom makes for spectacular shots rivaling crazy expensive cranes and jibs. But the entire setup is super lightweight. I bought my HX9V at Amazon.  For this application, I recommend the full length 10' Rode Boom Pole.  A couple of key accessories make this work:  Giottos MH1004-320 Mini Tripod Ball Head. This is a tiny ball head that is all you need to connect the HX9V to the Rode Boom.  The trickier part is monitoring. The HX9V outputs video via HDMI while recording, so monitoring is simply a matter of rigging a monitor to the boom pole.  I have a SmallHD DP6 monitor which I attached to the Rode Boom using a Manfrotto Magic Arm and a Manfrotto Super Clamp. This adds considerable bulk and weight, really too much for extended use and also the bulk really makes it difficult to move through crowds without bumping into people.  However, the spectacular lens and image stabilization of the HX9V make forvery compelling video. So much so, I am going to purchase a SmallHD DP4 EVF monitor for this rig. The Manfrotto mounting hardware has to go, however. I was not able to find anything through normal channels, so I started looking through bicycle specialty retailers for handlebar mounts. I've decided on a product called \\"RAM Mounts Roll Bar Mount Kit.\\" It looks very compact, is sized correctly to grip the Rode Boom Pole with a band, it has two articulated ball joints, and a tripod screw that should be perfect for the SmallHD DP4. Plus, I'm hoping the whole device will be rugged and strong since it is designed for jarring off road mountain biking.  A package of Bongo Ties, available from Amazon, used for cable management of the HDMI cable, completes the package.  Nothing is perfect, and it would be great to have remote control of the HX9V, especially start / stop recording. That's the only major downside of this rig - the fact that you have to haul the camera down to start or stop recording, which adds a bunch of garbage footage to the beginning and end of every shot. Still, I like it.  One other thing to keep an eye on is EV compensation. The HX9V does not have manual exposure control, which may sway some people to choose the NEX-5n or NEX-7, and the camera tends to overexpose 1/3 to 2/3rds of a stop. I spend too much time checking EV compensation while shooting; I need to figure out how to lock down this setting.  FWIW - I actually think the inexpensive HX9V is a better choice for this application than an NEX-5n or NEX-7, which are much more expensive cameras. I plan to buy an NEX-7 soon as it becomes available, but with other applications in mind. Riding the boom pole, the small sensor of the HX9V offers more insurance of sharp focus. Plus the HX9V 1080p 60fps video is spectacular slo mo, apparently the same as the NEX, though I yet have the NEX-7 and have not tested.  The HX9V is spectacular as a pole camera, and also as a handheld steadicam, frankly, another application for which I bought a $12 pistol grip from Amazon. Surprisingly, the audio from the built-in stereo mic is decent also, especially considering the pole cam is frequently used to get in very close quarters shooting where it would not be possible for a cameraman to normally be. One suggestion on audio - add a packet of Rycote Micro Windjammers to your kit to block wind noise. I had to fudge mine about a bit, cutting the adhesive patches to fit the stereo mic on the HX9V, but I think the end result is going to be good, though I have not yet tested outdoors.  One final thing: be sure to get a spare battery or two for the HX9V because this is an addictive way to shoot. The HX9V batteries can only be charged in camera, so you cannot charge while you shoot. Because the camera cannot be remote controlled, I tend to overshoot, and the batteries do not last terribly long. If I were a wedding videographer, I'd take at least 3 batteries to every shoot.

review_body: if you're waiting for some top off the line and under de budget headphones... try something else

product_title: Hohner Blues Band Seven-Piece Harmonica Set 1501
review_body: I've played harmonica off and on thru the years and recently decided to pick it up again, hearing greats like Neil Young and Al Wilson, adding the harp to my act, with voice and guitar doing covers and some of the \\"good\\" songs I've written. It's a greater advantage knowing keys of an instrument, harmonica included which I'm sure alot of people don't realize this and it's fully understandable. The Hohner Bluesband set is highly recommended from me and consist of seven keys, the majors,C,D,A,F,G,D, and Bb. The covers are stainless steel and each harp is the ten hole diatonic design, the sound is surprisingly good with probably medium volume. I've already blown a few blues with Neil Young,Pinetop Perkins, along with myself with voice and guitar with a holder. The outside cardboard cover provides a handy #key chart to play second position or \\"cross harp\\" blues. Think I'll wait a little longer to play along with Canned Heat's Al Wilson, the man was a maniac on harp. The drawback of this set is the key markings are painted and fade away easily with only a few light wipings, you'll have to eventually mark each harp with stickers and relabel the keys, the second drawback is this Hohner set is manufactured in China not Germany, for the money you can't go wrong, a great starter set for an upgrade, includes a good solid grey case.

product_title: First Note FN600 Firstnote Melody Harp
review_headline: Great introduction to music, for any age
review_body: You can get this for a three year old and you would be glad you did if he/she took an interest in it.  But if he/she does not take to it, perhaps you should wait for a year or two and then reintroduce him or her to it.  In any case you will be very glad you bought the product, as it let's you know whether your child, at an early age, has an interest or aptitude for it.  As a result of using the product, my grand-daughter of 6 is now studying the piano, and his brother of 9 is studying the guitar.  By the way, large harps are expensive, but worth while investing in them if a student is serious; you child will eventually be able to earn lots of money playing it.  Where? Weddings, funerals, many other solemn occasions. This small harp is an ideal way of seeing how serious someone really is, who has expressed an interest in music.

product_title: Sennheiser HD 280 Pro Headphones
review_body: Gift for husband and he likes them and I asked if he would order the same again and he said yes.

product_title: CC-J484 Catalina Club 4-Piece Jazz Shell Pack (White Marine)
review_body: This kit is trully amazing. I was at guitarcenter playing the kits when they were in the process of putting this one on display. I was the first one to play it, and I bought it after only 10 minutes of using it! All you need are some Evans G1 battered heads and your set. I play alternative music, and this jazz kit rocks like no other. Get this kit!

product_title: Hercules DS530B Alto/Tenor Sax Stand

The stand is compact so you can take it with you anywhere.  A must for every sax player.

review_body:
I facilitate local drum circles, and I am always looking to add new and interesting instruments (voices) to my percussion collection--especially those that allow children to participate without worry. While browsing on Amazon, I encountered this little version of the Festival djembe. Being an astronomy buff as well as a drummer, I just had to smile at a drum that had an artsy Constellation pattern...a snazzy splash of an idealized star map....a product that married my two loves into one with a color that rocks: purple! How cool is that! This well-made instrument can be enjoyed by children and adults alike. However, adults with large hands will find this little guy quite small, perhaps too small for comfortable. lengthy jamming. (For adults: think large Festival Djembe--you may even be able to find the large with the same color / pattern. Seems like I encountered a red one in my journeys in Amazon.)

Remo products are very much celebrated in percussion / drum healing-therapy circles, and they have inspired people to enter drum world / community. [Their sound shapes products ae great for small children too!] I am a fan of Remo and their products.

This Constellation drum has a sturdy, adjustable carrying strap that is really helpful when I need to move or take the instrument. To me, the drum isn't heavy. Notice though that there is often a relationship between small height and the playing surface--diameter of head. [Size can matter for some, especially when it comes to the instruments voice! :) ] Some customers may prefer an earthy \\"world / African style\\" djembe made from purely natural products--such as goat skin heads and wood bodies. In my research, I noticed several sellers encouraging buyers who want fully natural products to look for companies who only take materials from \\"legally harvested, sustainable forests.\\" A net search for \\"earth friendly djembe\\" or \\"environmental djembe\\" can bring the info to those who wish to know more.

According to the tag that came on this drum, the Acousticon drumshells are made with 100% Recycled Wood Fiber, and the product is said to be \\"Made in the USA.\\" The company states that their drums are \\"Durable, Portable, Playable, and Sustainable.\\" The little card also contains some other cool Eco facts about the company's efforts to be socially and environmentally responsible. These facts made me feel additionally good about this purchase.

I like the Remo drum and its FiberSkin & Acousticon material. The drum seems to have a distinct, pleasant, bright \\"voice\\" that inspires joy and dance. Its voice is different though from the world / African style djembes. So, before buying any instrument, do a bit of research to select the sound and style you like best. Remo's own product website can be helpful. The Amazon seller X8 Drums is also a fantastic source for those who wish to learn more about certain instruments; their website contains videos that show folks how to hold and play djembes.

review_body: What a toy for kids! It looks like a toy and functions like one, too. Useless! It's not sensitive. You've got to kiss it to make your voice heard thru amplifiers even if you tune the mike volume to max. And your voice doesn't mix in well with the instrumental either. It's cheap, indeed, but why waste $50(shipping included) on a piece of garbage? If I need a good mike, I'd have to spend more money anyway.   This $50 is just money lost.

product_title: Barcelona Beginner Series Electric Violin with Carrying Case and Accessories - White
review_body: This is a pretty solid Electric Violin. The plastic makes it light to hold, and that may be an issue for some as I like to feel the weight of an instrument to make it feel solid. The shoulder rest materials they give you are not worth installing, since they just fall off, and you would be better off to make your own, or buy one. Otherwise it sounds good and the headphone option is nice even though somehow this violin makes it's own reverberations without it, so you can also hear it without amplification or headphones, it just doesn't sound that good. Remember that if you have headphones on playing it next to someone.

product_title: The Singing Machine SMG-137 Top-Load CDG Karaoke System
review_body: My wife purchased one of these units before Christmas.  The intent was to use it during a family get together after Christmas.  When it arrived we hooked it up to our home tv, it did not work, the audio was fine but the words on the screen were all garbeled and illegible.  We took it with us the the party anyway, hoping it might work on a different tv.  It didn't, it had no video at all.  While playing around with the cables it was noticed that the unit would work only if the center pin on the RCA plug was touching the outer part of the receptacle on the unit.  In other words the RCA receptacle inside the unit must be wired backwards.  I tried to call the phone number listed in the directions but it was \\"no longer in service\\".  Sorry but we would not recommend this unit to anyone

product_title: Gallien-Krueger MB115 Ultralight Bass Guitar Combo (200 Wat)
review_body: I love this amp it's not expensive has tons of volume etc etc.  Played about 4 gigs with it so far and the only prob I have is the fact that sometimes the low lows can totally wash over the rhythm guitar player. >_< A slight annoyance that mainly comes from the fact that it uses a 15\\" sub. (15's pretty much can do lows and not so much in the higher range so everything has a lot of... well bass) If you have an extra 100 or 200$ I would recommend getting the model with 2 10\\"s or better yet the one up from that with 2 12\\"s.  Given the wattage and sub size on the other models the dynamic range is a lot better.  If you're not trying to go all out get this one you won't be disappointed.

product_title: Washburn Idol Series WI66PROFHBK Electric Guitar
review_body: Beautiful worksmanship, very clean sound, decent gig-bag. Plugged into a crate speaker and blackheart amp -- sounds very good across all settings (4 dials & dual seymour duncan pickups). Look on the Washburn site & Youtube -- almost all very favorable reviews. I got mine for high three hundreds, shipped and couldn't be happier

product_title: Sennheiser HD 280 Pro Headphones
review_body: Great headphones, let it run for atleast 100 hours, (aka burn-in) effect, then it sounds very good.    Only thing i do not like, it is very uncomfortable, very tight on the head. Hope Sennheiser will some design review on these headphones.    Other than that it is great!

product_title: Pignose Combo Wireless Microphone Wireless Microphone
review_body: The storage case tore and was not compact, so it is gone, but the product is quite nice.  I tried it out for voice recognition typing, and it seems to work up to around 20', around corners inside my house, and clearer, most of the time, than a direct connection.  It amplifies the microphone, and the sound is good.  For the price, it is remarkable.    I have noticed that, for hours, the voice recognition seems excellent, virtually without errors. Then, although the signal still seems strong and the batteries are good, I start seeing nonsense words.  I have not investigated further, but removing the wireless link at that point and making a direct connection resolves the problem. I look forward to using this product for sound recording and investigating possible variations in quality, but what I have seen so far makes me call it a nice, wireless solution for moderate distances, and for a fairly significant length of time.  With any device, important work should have suitable backup measures in place.
